pg008_n0005: This textbook, Food and Human Nutrition for Secondary Schools has been written specifically for Form One students in the United Republic of Tanzania.
pg008_n0006: The textbook has been prepared in accordance with the 2023 Food and Human Nutrition syllabus for Ordinary Secondary Education, Form I-IV, issued by the Ministry of Education Science and Technology (MoEST).
pg008_n0007: Furthermore, some of the contents are adapted from three textbooks, namely Home Economics for Secondary School, Student’s Book, Form Two (2021); Food and Human Nutrition, Student’s Book, Form Three; and Food and Human Nutrition Student’s Book, Form Four (2022) which were published in accordance with the 2019 syllabus issued by the Ministry of Education Science and Technology.
pg008_n0009: The textbook consists of seven (7) chapters, namely Introduction to food and nutrition; Food groups; The kitchen; Fruits and vegetables; Beverages and appetizers; Pulses, nuts and oil seeds; and Proper nutrition.
pg008_n0010: Besides, each chapter contains activities, illustrations, and exercises.
pg008_n0011: You are also required to prepare a portfolio for keeping records of the entire lessons.
pg008_n0012: You are encouraged to do all the activities and attempt all the questions.
pg008_n0013: Doing so will enhance your understanding and development of the intended competencies for this level.

pg009_n0008: Food and nutrition are essential components of human life and overall well-being.
pg009_n0009: Understanding the principles of food and nutrition is vital for making informed choices about the foods we eat and their impact on our bodies.
pg009_n0010: In this chapter, you will learn about the concept of food and nutrition, the importance of food, and the relationship between Food and Human Nutrition with other subjects.
pg009_n0011: The competencies developed will enable you to develop lifetime healthy eating behaviour and avoid nutrition-related health disorders.
pg009_n0014: Contribution of Food and Nutrition in our life
pg009_n0018: Food is anything edible that can be solid, semi-solid or liquid which when eaten, digested and assimilated in the body provides essential substances called nutrients.
pg009_n0019: Nutrients keep the person alive, provide energy, enable growth, repair worn-out tissues and protect the body from diseases.
pg009_n0020: Food is obtained from plants and animal sources.
pg009_n0021: It can be consumed in a raw state or in a processed form.
pg009_n0023: Nutrition is the process of taking in food and converting it into energy and other vital nutrients required for life.
pg009_n0024: It is concerned with how the body uses nutrients to nourish itself and perform different functions.
pg009_n0025: It is the study of all processes of growth, maintenance and repair of worn-out tissues in the body to remain healthy.
pg009_n0029: Understanding the functions of food is important in making informed dietary choices that support optimal health and well-being throughout life time.
pg009_n0030: The following are the importance of food:
pg010_n0003: Providing energy to the body: The body needs energy for various activities.
pg010_n0004: Carbohydrate and fat-rich foods are the main sources of energy for the body.
pg010_n0006: Building and repairing body cells and worn-out tissues: Body tissues are continually broken down and dying requiring repair and replacement to maintain overall health.
pg010_n0007: Foods rich in proteins, minerals and water are required to build and replace body cells and worn-out tissues.
pg010_n0009: Regulating body processes: Foods that contain fats, proteins, minerals, vitamins and water perform regulatory functions such as maintaining body temperature and activating enzymes.
pg010_n0011: Protecting the body against diseases: Food provides vitamins and minerals that protect the body from diseases.
pg010_n0012: Vitamins and minerals are also important in digestion and other body processes.
pg010_n0013: Examples of protective foods are fruits and vegetables.
pg010_n0015: Strengthening social relations: Eating food together creates an atmosphere where social relations can be developed.
pg010_n0016: Food helps in bringing people from different classes, communities and religions together.
pg010_n0018: Identification: Food can be used to identify individuals from different backgrounds such as ethnic and or cultural backgrounds.
pg010_n0019: For example, the preference for bananas among the people of Bukoba and Kilimanjaro illustrates part of their cultural identity.
pg010_n0023: Food can be classified based on the function it performs in the body, its chemical composition, the chemical properties of nutrients and its source or origin.
pg010_n0025: Classification of food based on the function it performs in the body
pg010_n0027: Considering this criterion, foods are classified as energy-giving foods, body-building foods and protective foods.
pg010_n0029: Energy-giving foods: Foods rich in carbohydrates and fats provide energy, which is essential for performing physical activities and the basic functioning of the body.
pg010_n0030: These foods are called energy-giving foods.
pg010_n0031: Foods that are good sources of energy include cereals, roots, tubers, and fats, such as butter, ghee and oils.
pg010_n0033: Body-building foods: One of the most important functions of food is building the body.
pg010_n0034: Foods rich in protein are called body-building foods.
pg010_n0035: These foods help to maintain life and promote growth and repair of damaged body tissues.
pg011_n0003: foods come from animals and plants.
pg011_n0004: Good sources of animal protein include milk, meat, eggs and fish while good sources of plant protein include pulses and nuts.
pg011_n0005: Animal protein sources are considered to be of higher quality than plant protein sources, except for soybeans which contain higher-quality protein.
pg011_n0007: Protective foods: Foods rich in minerals and vitamins are known as protective foods.
pg011_n0008: They protect the body against diseases.
pg011_n0009: Examples of protective foods include fruits and vegetables.
pg011_n0011: Classification of food based on its chemical composition
pg011_n0013: The chemical composition of food is important since it determines its utilization in the body.
pg011_n0014: This classification is based on the types and amount of nutrients present in the food.
pg011_n0015: Carbohydrates, proteins and lipids form the major chemical components of foods since they are available in large quantities.
pg011_n0016: Vitamins and minerals form the minor chemical components of food since they are present in smaller quantities in foods.
pg011_n0018: Classification of food based on the chemical properties of nutrients
pg011_n0020: Under this type of classification, food is classified based on the chemical properties of nutrients such as organic and inorganic nutrients.
pg011_n0021: Nutrients such as carbohydrates, protein, fat and vitamins contain elements of carbon.
pg011_n0022: These are called organic nutrients; and nutrients that do not contain carbon elements such as minerals are called inorganic nutrients.
pg011_n0024: Classification of food based on its origin
pg011_n0026: Depending on its origin, food can be classified based on the sources.
pg011_n0027: Foods which are obtained from animals are called animal food sources, whereas foods from plants are called plant food sources.

pg012_n0042: Relationship between Food and Human Nutrition with other subjects
pg012_n0044: Food and Human Nutrition, and Mathematics: Food and Human Nutrition applies knowledge and skills from other subjects which relate to it.
pg012_n0045: For example, measuring the amount of ingredients needed to prepare a healthy and nutritious meal involves the application of Mathematics.
pg012_n0047: Food and Human Nutrition, and Physics: Food and Human Nutrition is also related to Physics in several aspects.
pg012_n0048: A good example is cooking food using a pressure cooker.
pg012_n0049: As water boils, steam is produced, pressure increases and the boiling point is raised.
pg012_n0050: The higher temperature and pressure inside the cooker enable the food to cook very quickly.
pg012_n0051: This is an application of Physics.
pg012_n0052: Similarly, cooking pots, cookers, microwaves and refrigerators are designed to work under the principles of Physics.
pg013_n0003: Food and Human Nutrition, and Chemistry: To understand the functions of various nutrients in our body, one needs to learn the elements contained in carbohydrates, proteins, and minerals.
pg013_n0004: This involves the application of Chemistry.
pg013_n0005: On the other hand, through Chemistry, one learns how to make bleaches and detergents which are used as cleaning agents in cleaning kitchen cloths and equipment.
pg013_n0007: Food and Human Nutrition, and Biology: In Biology people learn the role of nutrients in the body and the effects of their deficiency.
pg013_n0008: They also learn about food preservation to prevent spoilage and diseases.
pg013_n0009: Such knowledge is applied during food preparation and cooking in Food and Human Nutrition.
pg013_n0011: Food and Human Nutrition, and Economics: Economic factors such as food prices and income influence people’s food choices.
pg013_n0012: Food budgeting is essential before preparing food.
pg013_n0013: The application of knowledge from Economics is required in food budgeting, especially when planning meals because one should consider the amount of money available before purchasing food items.
pg013_n0014: Knowledge of Economics enables an individual to understand that food preparation should always match with the money available.
pg013_n0015: Economics is also useful in managing time, money and energy during planning, preparing, cooking and serving food, as well as when buying food from the market.
pg013_n0017: Food and Human Nutrition, and Agriculture: Food and Human Nutrition also relate to Agriculture since foods for human consumption are obtained from the farm.
pg013_n0018: Growing foods requires an individual to know something about agriculture.
pg013_n0019: Such foods involve fruits and vegetables, which are used in making beverages and appetizers.
pg013_n0020: Likewise, producing animal-based food products, such as milk, fish, eggs and meat requires the knowledge of Agriculture.

pg014_n0008: A food group is a collection of foods that share similar nutritional properties.
pg014_n0009: Foods are grouped together because they consist similar nutrients.
pg014_n0010: For example, nutrients in cheese, milk and yoghurt include calcium and protein.
pg014_n0011: In this chapter, you will learn about the concept of food groups, nutrients present in different foods and a balanced meal.
pg014_n0012: The competencies developed will enable you to make proper food choices, prepare a balanced meal and retain the nutrients present in food during food preparation, cooking and serving.
pg014_n0015: Meal planning without using food groups
pg014_n0019: Foods are divided into groups based on the types and nutrients they provide.
pg014_n0020: Therefore, when planning meals, you should include a variety of foods from all food groups to prepare balanced meals.
pg014_n0021: The main food groups include the following:
pg014_n0025: Cereals, starchy, roots, tubers, plantains and green bananas: Examples include wheat, millet, sorghum, rice, maize, Irish potatoes, cassava, yams and green bananas.
pg014_n0026: They mainly supply carbohydrates for energy provision in the body.
pg014_n0029: Foods of animal origin: These include foods such as chicken, eggs, milk, fish, beef.
pg014_n0030: These foods provide mainly protein for building and repairing cells and tissues.
pg014_n0033: Vegetables: This group include foods such as green leafy vegetables (amaranths, sweet potato leaves, pumpkin leaves, and cassava leaves), tomatoes, carrots, eggplants and sweet peppers.
pg014_n0034: Vegetables mainly provide vitamins and minerals to strengthen the immune system.
pg015_n0003: (d) Fruits: This group include foods such as pineapples, oranges, mangoes, papayas, baobab fruit, tamarind, avocado, guava and lemons.
pg015_n0004: They provide mainly vitamins and minerals to strengthen the immune system.
pg015_n0006: (e) Pulses, Nuts and Oily seeds: This group include food such as green gram, cowpeas, cashewnuts, groundnuts and sunflower seeds.
pg015_n0007: Pulses and Nuts are good sources of protein, vitamins and minerals.
pg015_n0008: Oily seeds provide oil which provide energy in our body.
pg015_n0010: (f) Fats and oils: This group include foods such as margarine, butter, palm oil, sesame oil, coconut oil and sunflower oil.
pg015_n0011: Fats and oil provide energy to the body.

pg016_n0027: Nutrients are chemical substances present in food that must be supplied to the body in suitable amounts.
pg016_n0028: The amount of nutrients needed by the body depends on the age, sex, activity, and physiological and health condition of an individual.
pg016_n0029: Nutrients include carbohydrates, proteins, fats, minerals, and vitamins.
pg016_n0030: Water is not a nutrient, but it is used in the digestion and absorption process of nutrients.
pg016_n0031: Likewise, dietary fibre, also known as roughage, is not a nutrient; but it is needed in the digestion process.
pg016_n0032: The body needs a wide range of nutrients to remain healthy and maintain life.
pg016_n0033: Most foods contain more than one nutrient.
pg016_n0034: For example, milk contains protein, fats, vitamins and minerals.
pg016_n0035: Nutrients are categorised into two main groups, namely macronutrients and micronutrients, based on the body’s requirements.
pg016_n0039: These are required in large amounts in the body.
pg016_n0040: They include carbohydrates, proteins and fats.
pg017_n0003: Carbohydrates: These are food substances that are composed of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen atoms.
pg017_n0004: They produce most of the energy needed in the body; hence, they are referred to as energy-giving foods.
pg017_n0005: Plants are the main source of carbohydrates.
pg017_n0006: There are two forms of carbohydrates, namely starches and sugars.
pg017_n0010: Starches: These include foods from cereals, tubers and starchy fruits.
pg017_n0011: Cereals include rice, wheat, sorghum and millet.
pg017_n0012: Roots and tubers include Irish potatoes, yams and cassava, and starchy fruits such as green bananas.
pg017_n0015: Sugars: These include foods such as honey, table sugar, and sugarcane.
pg017_n0017: Functions of carbohydrates in the body
pg017_n0019: The major functions of carbohydrates in the body are to
pg017_n0023: provide energy to the body for different activities;
pg017_n0026: assist in lipid metabolism, a process of breaking down fats which is used to facilitate various body functions; and
pg017_n0030: Carbohydrates are broken down to release energy, contributing to warmth.
pg017_n0032: Proteins: These consist of carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen and oxygen atoms.
pg017_n0033: Nitrogen forms an important component of proteins because it is needed for making all cells in the body.
pg017_n0034: Some common protein food sources include dairy products, legumes and nuts.
pg017_n0035: Protein is essential for the growth of the body and repair of worn-out cells.
pg017_n0036: The building blocks of protein are amino acids.
pg017_n0037: There are two types of amino acids, which are essential amino acids and non-essential amino acids.
pg017_n0038: Essential amino acids are obtained from the food we eat.
pg017_n0039: Non-essential amino acids are synthesized in the body.
pg017_n0040: Protein, which contains all essential amino acids, is called complete protein, also known as protein of a high biological value or first class protein.
pg017_n0041: Complete protein is mostly found in animal food sources such as milk, meat, fish, poultry and eggs.
pg017_n0042: A protein which does not contain all essential amino acids is called incomplete protein, also known as a low biological value protein or second-class protein.
pg017_n0043: Incomplete protein is commonly found in plant food sources such as pulses and nuts.
pg018_n0003: Functions of proteins in the body
pg018_n0005: Proteins perform the following functions in the body:
pg018_n0009: Development of body tissues, maintenance or repair and replacement of worn-out tissues;
pg018_n0011: (ii) Formation of enzymes and hormones for regulating body processes;
pg018_n0013: (iii) Production of antibodies, which help the body to fight against diseases, and
pg018_n0015: (iv) Supplying the body with energy when a meal does not provide enough carbohydrates and fats.
pg018_n0017: Fats: These are food substances composed of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen atoms, like in carbohydrates but in different proportions.
pg018_n0018: Fats are the most concentrated energy foods found in both animals and plants.
pg018_n0019: Animal fat foods include poultry and dairy products such as butter, cheese, and fatty fish such as salmon.
pg018_n0020: Vegetable oils include oils from sunflower and cotton seeds and palm and coconut.
pg018_n0022: Functions of fats in the body
pg018_n0026: The layer of fat under the skin controls heat loss from the body to the environment, thus maintaining body temperature.
pg018_n0028: (ii) Fats protect internal organs, such as the heart and kidneys, from damage.
pg018_n0030: (iii) They provide a sense of fullness.
pg018_n0031: Fats take longer to digest than carbohydrates and proteins do.
pg018_n0032: Therefore, when included in a meal, fats can slow down digestion.
pg018_n0034: (iv) Fats are a concentrated source of energy.
pg018_n0035: Foods rich in fat provide high energy value.
pg018_n0037: (v) They provide a reserve of energy for long-term storage, which can be utilised if the energy intake is reduced or stopped.
pg018_n0039: (vi) Fats improve the texture and flavour of foods.
pg018_n0041: (vii) They facilitate the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E and K) in the body.
pg019_n0005: They are required by the body in small amounts.
pg019_n0007: Although micro-nutrients are needed in small amounts, they are essential for the body to function well.
pg019_n0009: Vitamins: These are chemical compounds that the body needs in small amounts to help it function properly.
pg019_n0010: Although they are needed in small amounts, they are essential for various bodily processes and overall health.
pg019_n0011: Inadequate supply of vitamins in the diet may result in deficiency disorders.
pg019_n0013: Vitamins are classified into two groups, as follows:
pg019_n0017: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K)
pg019_n0022: These vitamins are soluble in fats and are stored in the body’s cells.
pg019_n0023: An adequate amount of these nutrients should be taken.
pg019_n0024: Consumption of excess amounts of fat-soluble vitamins may become toxic to the body.
pg019_n0026: These vitamins are soluble in water; the body needs them daily in recommended amounts.
pg019_n0027: Water-soluble vitamins are not stored in the body.
pg019_n0028: The excess amounts of water-soluble vitamins are excreted through urine.
pg019_n0029: Hence, it is not likely to reach toxic levels.

pg025_n0056: Water: This is vital for life.
pg025_n0057: It should be taken every day, especially in hot weather where large amounts of water are lost through sweating.
pg025_n0058: About two-thirds of the body’s weight is water.
pg025_n0059: The body requires water frequently for the following reasons:
pg025_n0062: (i) Forming an essential component in blood and body secretions such as digestive juices;
pg025_n0064: (ii) Carrying nutrients and oxygen to body cells;
pg025_n0066: (iii) Supporting the structure of body cells;
pg025_n0068: (iv) Assisting in food digestion, absorption and assimilation of nutrients;
pg025_n0070: (v) Assisting in the secretion and elimination of body wastes through the kidneys;
pg026_n0011: Acting as a lubricant in joints and membranes.
pg026_n0015: Dietary fibre or roughage is a part of food that is not digested in the body.
pg026_n0016: It is found in plant foods.
pg026_n0017: Good sources of dietary fibre include unrefined cereals such as wheat, maize and oats.
pg026_n0018: It is also found in the cell walls of fruits such as apples, plums, and in pears and vegetables, especially leafy vegetables like celery, amaranths and cabbage.
pg026_n0019: Nuts, oil seeds and pulses such as peas, beans and lentils also contain dietary fibre.
pg026_n0020: The following points show the importance of dietary fibre in the body:
pg026_n0025: Insoluble fibre tends to speed up the passage of foods through the gastro intestinal tract and add bulk to the stool reducing constipation and lowers the risk of colon cancer.
pg026_n0028: It lowers cholesterol and blood glucose levels, thus helping to prevent the risk of diseases such as diabetes and heart diseases.
pg026_n0031: It speeds up the passage of food through the digestive tract, hence increasing the faecal bulk.
pg026_n0035: The consumption of foods that contain high amounts of dietary fibre, such as fruits and vegetables, regulates body weight since they have few calories.

pg027_n0019: Different foods contain different types of nutrients, which can be altered through food preparation, cooking and storage.
pg027_n0020: Therefore, retention of nutrients during these processes is important.
pg027_n0021: This will help in preventing nutrient loss.
pg027_n0025: During food preparation, food may come in contact with water, heat and air.
pg027_n0026: These elements may affect the stability of food nutrients.
pg027_n0027: There may be noticeable changes in appearance, texture, and flavour.
pg027_n0028: Nutritive values of foods may also be affected when subjected to different food preparation methods.
pg027_n0029: For example, allowing leafy vegetables to remain soaked in washing water or shredding them too thinly can lead to a loss of water-soluble vitamins (vitamin B group and C).
pg027_n0030: Vitamin B₁ can also be lost through washing rice.
pg027_n0031: Soaking rice in water allows certain B vitamins to leach into the water.
pg027_n0032: Exposing fruit juices to air may result in the loss of vitamin C.
pg028_n0003: Retention of nutrients during foods preparation can be done in the following ways:
pg028_n0007: When peeling foods like potatoes, carrots and fruits, use a sharp knife to peel them thinly to avoid losing the nutrients found under the peel.
pg028_n0010: Wash fruits and vegetables before chopping to avoid loss of vitamins through leaching into the water.
pg028_n0011: Use a sharp knife when chopping.
pg028_n0014: Avoid exposing vegetables to direct sunlight to prevent the loss of vitamins, such as vitamin C.
pg028_n0017: Fruits and vegetables should be prepared just a few minutes before serving.
pg028_n0020: Fruits and vegetables should not be soaked because water-soluble vitamins can leach into the soaking water.
pg028_n0024: When some foods are cooked in water, nutrients are dissolved in them.
pg028_n0025: If the water is discarded, these nutrients are lost.
pg028_n0026: Cooking leafy vegetables for too long can destroy some vitamins.
pg028_n0028: The retention of nutrients during cooking can be done in the following ways:
pg028_n0032: Cook leafy vegetables for a short period, just before serving and avoid overcooking as it will cause loss of some nutrients.
pg028_n0035: Cook food with little water and serve the food with its liquid to avoid losing water-soluble vitamins.
pg028_n0038: Prepare enough food for a moment to avoid leftovers which will need reheating, causing loss of nutrients.
pg028_n0041: It is advisable to cook vegetables for a short time to reduce the loss of heat-sensitive nutrients such as B vitamins and vitamin C.
pg028_n0044: Cover the food when cooking as some of the water-soluble vitamins like B-vitamins and vitamin C can evaporate.
pg028_n0047: Do not use bicarbonate of soda or ashes in cooking as they destroy many vitamins, such as vitamins C, D, B<math><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and B<math><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></math>.

pg029_n0005: It also tends to facilitate the loss of iodine.
pg029_n0006: Exposure of milk to the sun leads to the loss of B-vitamins.
pg029_n0008: The retention of nutrients during food storage can be done in the following ways:
pg029_n0012: Fruits and vegetables should be stored for a short time to maintain their freshness, nutrients, flavour and overall quality.
pg029_n0015: Keep milk in covered and coloured containers to prevent loss of vitamin B2.
pg029_n0018: Store food in a cool environment away from direct sunlight as this can lead to loss of nutrients such as vitamins B2 and C.

pg030_n0005: A meal refers to all foods eaten at one time or on one occasion, such as breakfast, lunch or supper.
pg030_n0006: A meal is made up of different dishes.
pg030_n0007: A dish is a food prepared in a particular way as part of the meal.
pg030_n0008: A balanced meal comprises a variety of foods from all food groups.
pg030_n0009: It should contain adequate amounts and proportions of nutrients needed by the body for growth, repairing damaged tissues and maintaining good health.
pg030_n0010: These nutrients are carbohydrates, fats, proteins, minerals and vitamins.
pg030_n0011: Since no single food can provide all nutrients in the right amount, good nutrition depends on getting a variety of different foods from all food groups.
pg030_n0012: In addition, one should consider enough water and roughage as important contents in a balanced meal.

pg031_n0006: A balanced meal is very important to the body as it comprises of foods from all food groups that provide essential nutrients for growth, repair of damaged body tissues and strengthening the body’s immune system to prevent the body against diseases.
pg031_n0007: It is important to eat a balanced meal at least three times a day to ensure adequate intake of all nutrients needed for normal functioning of the body.
pg031_n0008: A balanced meal also helps in preventing depression and anxiety and improves thinking capacity.
pg031_n0009: Likewise, a balanced meal promotes the growth and development of children and adolescents who are still in the growth stage.
pg031_n0010: For elderly people, a balanced meal helps to maintain and repair worn-out tissues.
pg031_n0012: Factors to consider when planning balanced meals for family members
pg031_n0014: Meals should be planned for all family members to get appropriate foods with nutrients in the right proportions to meet dietary preferences and nutritional requirements.
pg031_n0015: One should consider the following points when planning family meals:
pg031_n0017: Nutrient adequacy: It is important to ensure that the meal contains all the nutrients.
pg031_n0018: This is achieved by including foods from all groups.
pg031_n0019: Dietary fibre should also be considered during meal planning as it aids in digestion.
pg031_n0021: Food variety: Food variety is important to avoid food monotony and dietary deficiency in addition to making the dish appetising.
pg031_n0022: This can be achieved by using various cooking methods and including foods with different flavours, textures, and colours.
pg031_n0024: Seasonal availability of food: It is wise to choose foods that are in season because they are fresh, nutritious, and cheap.
pg031_n0025: Off-season foods tend to be expensive.
pg031_n0026: Besides, most of them may lack freshness, because they have been processed or stored for a long time.
pg031_n0027: Examples of seasonal foods are vegetables and fruits.
pg031_n0029: Individual body needs: This includes age, sex, occupation of an individual and the state of the body.
pg031_n0035: The meal prepared should consider the age of each family member because nutritional requirements differ based on respective lifecycle stages such as children, adolescents, adults and the elderly.
pg031_n0036: For example, children need more protein foods than adults do due to their rapid growth.
pg031_n0041: The sex of an individual can influence the planning for meals.
pg031_n0042: Women of Reproductive Age (WRA) require more iron-rich foods than men do to replace the blood lost during menstruation.
pg031_n0043: Usually, adolescents and adult males require more energy than females do.
pg032_n0004: The meal prepared should meet the needs of the body according to the kind of work the individual performs.
pg032_n0005: For example, sedentary workers require less energy-giving foods than manual workers.
pg032_n0006: (iv) State of the body or physiological status
pg032_n0008: This factor includes different conditions the body experiences such as disease, pregnancy, and lactation.
pg032_n0009: These conditions affect food intake and nutrient metabolism.
pg032_n0010: For example, sick people require more proteins and vitamins to aid the recovery process and strengthen their immune systems.
pg032_n0011: Whereas type 2 diabetic patients do not need high sugary foods in their diets; pregnant women need more folate and iron in their meals to prevent birth defects and anaemia.
pg032_n0014: The choice of family food to be prepared will also be determined by the time available for shopping, preparing, cooking and serving food.
pg032_n0015: For example, one can plan to prepare fresh beans instead of dry beans because the latter needs to be cooked for a long time.
pg032_n0016: An individual with a gas or an electrical cooker can prepare many dishes in a short time.
pg032_n0017: In contrast, the one using a charcoal stove may not do so, unless he or she uses multiple charcoal stoves at once.
pg032_n0020: The budget allocated for family meals determines the type, quality and quantity of food to be purchased.
pg032_n0021: For many families, foods such as beef, chicken and fish can be too expensive for their budgets.
pg032_n0022: Hence, a family can buy alternative foods such as sardines or offal which contain similar nutrients.
pg032_n0025: One should consider the kitchenware and equipment available for preparing, cooking and serving foods as well as storage facilities.
pg032_n0028: A meal should be prepared according to the prevailing weather conditions.
pg032_n0029: For example, foods that are served hot such as soup and tea are preferable to keep the body warm in cold weather conditions.
pg032_n0032: Meals should be planned based on the appropriate time of the day, such as morning, afternoon, or evening.
pg032_n0033: For example, supper should be light because a person is preparing to go to bed.
pg032_n0034: Night time requires little energy since the body will be resting.
pg032_n0036: Religion, cultural values, traditional beliefs and taboos:
pg032_n0037: Religion, cultural values, traditional beliefs and taboos determine what should be cooked and eaten.
pg032_n0038: In planning for meals, one should consider these beliefs to prepare meals that are acceptable in the family or locality.

pg035_n0008: The kitchen is one of the important places found at home.
pg035_n0009: It should be well equipped to facilitate efficient preparation and cooking of food.
pg035_n0010: In this chapter, you will learn about the kitchen, hygiene in food preparation and cooking and safety in the kitchen.
pg035_n0011: The competencies developed will enable you to take proper care of the kitchen to avoid accidents and to prepare, cook, and serve food hygienically.
pg035_n0017: A kitchen is a room or an area inside or outside the house or commercial establishment where food is prepared, cooked, and sometimes served.
pg035_n0018: Other related activities such as washing utensils are also performed in the kitchen.
pg035_n0019: It should be well-planned to increase efficiency and to save time and energy.
pg035_n0020: When the kitchen is well planned, the utensils are in appropriate order to form a continuous working area which suits the sequence and stages of the main activities to be carried out in the kitchen.
pg035_n0021: It is important to arrange fixed equipment in sequence to suit the activities carried out in the kitchen to save time for work and avoid unnecessary movements.
pg035_n0022: It can be built either inside or outside the main house.
pg035_n0025: Two main types of kitchens are commonly found in residential settings.
pg035_n0026: These are open kitchens and separate kitchens.
pg036_n0005: In this type, the kitchen is openly seen from the dining or living room.
pg036_n0006: There is no separate wall, partition or door.
pg036_n0007: Open kitchens allow hosts or cooks to interact with guests while preparing meals.
pg036_n0008: With an open kitchen, it is easy to prepare and replace meals and remove dirty utensils from the dining table.
pg036_n0009: It is also easy to see unwashed dishes, scattered utensils and food scraps.
pg036_n0010: Therefore, this type of kitchen requires constant cleaning to maintain kitchen hygiene.
pg036_n0011: There are two types of open kitchen, as described below:
pg036_n0013: Kitchen open to the dining room: In this type, the kitchen opens to the dining.
pg036_n0014: There is neither a separate wall nor a door, and someone can see everything in the kitchen from the dining room, as shown in Figure 3.1.
pg036_n0015: Usually, there is no privacy during meal preparation because people who are seated in the dining room can see food preparation and cooking in the kitchen.

pg036_n0019: Kitchen open to the living room: In this type, the kitchen is combined with the living room.
pg036_n0020: It can be seen clearly from the living room.
pg036_n0021: This type of kitchen gives convenience for other activities such as watching television or spending time with other family members or guests while preparing meals.

pg037_n0007: This type of kitchen can be built within the main house (enclosed) or outside the main house (isolated).
pg037_n0008: A separate kitchen always gives privacy during meal preparation and prevents heat, steam and smoke from infiltrating into the house.
pg037_n0009: Separate kitchens provide a more traditional and functional set up, ideal for those who prefer a clear division between cooking and living spaces.

pg038_n0007: A good kitchen has several key qualities that make it efficient, functional and enjoyable to work in.
pg038_n0008: The following are qualities of a good kitchen:
pg038_n0012: The kitchen which is positioned in the manner that allows enough sunlight and air to enter.
pg038_n0015: Kitchen walls furnished with smooth and easy-to-clean material.
pg038_n0016: Colours in the kitchen walls, including the ceiling should be bright to reflect light in the room.
pg038_n0019: The kitchen floor made up of non-slippery materials that are easy to clean such as cement and tiles.
pg039_n0010: The kitchen with large equipment such as cookers, sinks, cupboards and refrigerators placed in convenient places for quick and easy movement.
pg039_n0013: Kitchen with windows large enough for proper air circulation.
pg039_n0014: Ventilation is important because it removes smoke, smell and excess heat from the kitchen.
pg039_n0017: The kitchen with adequate lighting for safe food preparation and cooking.
pg039_n0018: A good kitchen allows both natural and artificial lighting to see clearly during the day and night.
pg039_n0021: The kitchen with a sink fixed with taps giving a good supply of both hot and cold water.
pg039_n0022: It should be fitted directly under the kitchen window to enable the user to get enough natural light and fresh air while working at the sink.
pg039_n0025: The kitchen with a good drainage system is that ensures kitchen hygiene.
pg039_n0028: The kitchen with a wastebin for collecting garbage.

pg040_n0005: Kitchen equipment refers to various tools, appliances and utensils used in food preparation, cooking, and other culinary tasks.
pg040_n0006: Having the right kitchen equipment can make cooking more efficient and enjoyable.
pg040_n0007: There are large, small and labour-saving pieces of equipment.
pg040_n0008: Large pieces of equipment include cookers, refrigerators and cupboards.
pg040_n0009: Small pieces of kitchen equipment are grouped as:
pg040_n0012: (i) wooden equipment such as chopping boards, wooden spoons, pastry boards and rolling pins;
pg040_n0014: (ii) serving equipment such as glasses, cups, serving spoons and plates;
pg040_n0016: (iii) measuring equipment such as measuring scales, jugs and spoons;
pg040_n0018: (iv) baking tins such as patty tins, cake baking tins, sandwich baking tins and loaf baking tin;
pg040_n0020: (v) cutlery items such as table spoons, forks, dessert spoons and tea spoons; and
pg040_n0022: (vi) knives such as chopping knives, bread knives, paring knives and vegetable knives
pg040_n0024: Labour-saving equipment are appliances that help one to speed up food preparation, cooking and serving to save time and energy.
pg040_n0025: These devices are intended to increase efficiency and productivity, allowing people to accomplish tasks more quickly and with less physical effort.
pg040_n0026: Some examples of labour-saving equipment in the kitchen include a microwave oven, food processor, dishwasher, electric mixer, blender, deep fryer, rice cooker, pressure cooker, electric kettle and sandwich maker.

pg044_n0003: Hygiene in food preparation and cooking
pg044_n0005: Kitchen hygiene is important in maintaining food safety and preventing the spread of infectious diseases.
pg044_n0006: Proper hygiene in the kitchen helps to ensure that the food is prepared and handled safely, reducing the risk of food contamination and the growth of harmful micro-organisms.
pg044_n0007: Therefore, one should consider kitchen, personal and food hygiene when preparing, cooking and serving food.
pg044_n0009: Kitchen hygiene: This refers to the cleanliness of kitchen surfaces and equipment and the proper disposal of kitchen refuse to avoid food contamination.
pg044_n0010: A dirty kitchen produces an unpleasant smell and encourages the growth and multiplication of germs and pests, which are dangerous to health; they cause diseases.
pg044_n0011: A dirty kitchen may cause falling down accidents due to spillage of water, oil or food on the kitchen floor.
pg044_n0012: To keep the kitchen clean and hygienic, one should observe the following rules:
pg044_n0016: Ensure the kitchen is well-ventilated to avoid bad smells and pests.
pg044_n0019: Wash all utensils immediately after use and dry them accordingly.
pg044_n0022: Clean all areas, including working surfaces with soap and water whenever it is dirty.
pg044_n0025: Sweep and mop the floor often as the kitchen gets greasy and dirty.
pg044_n0028: Often wash kitchen cloths with soap and warm water, dry them in the sun and iron them to kill germs.
pg044_n0031: Inspect the kitchen for any plumbing leaks all the time to ensure proper drainage.
pg044_n0034: Wrap all the refuse before throwing it into the bin.
pg044_n0037: Use a covered waste bin to dispose of kitchen waste.
pg044_n0038: Empty the bin regularly to prevent odours and pests.
pg044_n0039: Clean and disinfect the waste bin occasionally.
pg044_n0041: Food hygiene: Food hygiene refers to conditions and measures which make food safe for consumption. The food should be prepared, cooked and stored properly to avoid contamination and poisoning. The following are the points to consider in food hygiene:
pg044_n0045: Cover or wrap the food well before storing it in a cool and proper place so that it does not attract pests and pets.
pg044_n0046: Household pets carry microorganisms which may contaminate food in the kitchen.
pg044_n0049: Use separate cutting boards for raw and cooked foods such as meat, poultry and vegetables to avoid cross-contamination.
pg045_n0006: Wash cooking pots and serving dishes with warm water and soap and rinse with running water.
pg045_n0009: Avoid leaving perishable foods at room temperature for extended periods as it may cause moisture loss and attract spoilage microorganisms.
pg045_n0012: Store different foods at their proper places to avoid spoilage that can bring a bad smell to the kitchen.
pg045_n0015: Isolate raw foods from ready-to-eat foods to prevent cross-contamination.
pg045_n0018: Cook thoroughly all foods that require cooking.
pg045_n0021: Thaw the frozen food before cooking to have adequate heat penetration to the food.
pg045_n0024: Use clean and safe water for cooking food.
pg045_n0027: Keep the food at the right temperature to avoid spoilage.
pg045_n0030: Wash fruits and vegetables thoroughly, especially those that are eaten raw, with clean and safe running water.
pg045_n0033: Personal hygiene in the kitchen is important to maintain food safety and prevent food contamination and poisoning.
pg045_n0034: Food handlers should observe the following hygienic practices:
pg045_n0038: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and clean water before handling food and after visiting the toilet.
pg045_n0041: Avoid touching clothes, the nose, mouth, hair, or any body part when preparing food as bacteria can get into contact with the food.
pg045_n0042: Always cover your mouth and nose with a handkerchief when coughing or sneezing.
pg045_n0045: Remove jewellery like rings and watches before handling food to prevent trapping bacteria.
pg045_n0048: Wear protective clothing such as an apron to avoid getting dirty and cover your hair with a hat or head scarf to prevent food from being contaminated by micro-organisms.
pg045_n0051: Keep your finger nails short because long nails harbour microorganisms.
pg045_n0054: Cover cuts, sores or wounds with clean sterile and water proof bandages while preparing and cooking food.
pg046_n0003: (g) Wear shoes in the kitchen to protect the body from accidents such as falling.
pg046_n0004: Wearing shoes also prevents you from being contaminated by bacteria and food particles found in the kitchen.

pg048_n0040: The kitchen can be a place with numerous potential hazards and accidents if proper safety measures are not followed.
pg048_n0041: Accidents such as burns, scalds, fires, and cuts commonly occur in the kitchen.
pg048_n0043: Burns: These can result from contact with hot surfaces such as pots, pans and cookers or hot liquids such as oil.
pg048_n0044: For example, a pan of oil that gets too hot can ignite and cause burns to the person who tries to put it off.
pg048_n0045: To avoid burns, use pot holders to
pg049_n0006: Likewise, use oven gloves to pull out racks from the oven when removing dishes after cooking.
pg049_n0008: If burns occur, cool the whole area with cold water for several minutes to reduce the pain and lower the risk of blistering.
pg049_n0009: If blisters occur, do not break them.
pg049_n0010: Apply some petroleum jelly and avoid exposure of the burnt area to the air as it will cause more pain.
pg049_n0011: Minor burns can be covered with sterile gauze and bandages.
pg049_n0014: These are caused by burning with hot liquid such as hot water or steam.
pg049_n0015: For example, a hot steam which comes from food can also cause scalds.
pg049_n0016: To prevent scalds, keep boiling pots stable and turn their handles away from the cooker.
pg049_n0017: Use pot holders when removing pans or pots from the cooker.
pg049_n0018: When opening lids while cooking, make sure that you direct the steam away from you.
pg049_n0019: If scalds occur, deep the injured part in cold water.
pg049_n0020: This will cool the body and, hence, reduce the pain.
pg049_n0021: Do not break the blisters as they protect the injured part from bacterial infection.
pg049_n0022: Apply petroleum jelly on the scalds.
pg049_n0025: Fire in the kitchen can result from a leakage of a gas pipe or from coming in contact with materials which can catch fire like curtains or kitchen cloths.
pg049_n0026: Unintentionally turning on or leaving the cooker on may also cause a fire.
pg049_n0027: To minimize this risk, always unplug electrical appliances or put off cooking stoves after use.
pg049_n0028: Never pour water on a grease fire.
pg049_n0029: Instead, use a large pan lid to prevent the fire from spreading.
pg049_n0030: Covering the fire with a damp towel can also extinguish the fire.
pg049_n0031: If you smell gas, turn off all gas jets and open the windows to disperse any built-up gas.
pg049_n0032: Light the match first before turning on the gas when lighting the gas cooker.
pg049_n0033: Do not store anything attractive to children near the cooker, such as snacks.
pg049_n0034: Keep all items such as kitchen cloths and curtains away from the cooker.
pg049_n0035: It is a good practice to have a fire extinguisher available for use but not for grease fire as it can spray or shoot the burning grease around the kitchen, thus spreading the fire.
pg049_n0036: Keep children and pets away from cooking areas to minimize the risk of accidents that might lead to fire.
pg049_n0039: You should do chopping or cutting of food items carefully to avoid cutting your hand and causing injuries.
pg049_n0040: Do not put knives and sharp objects together with other utensils during washing.
pg049_n0041: Broken glasses in the kitchen can also cause cuts.
pg049_n0042: If cuts occur, clean the wound with a weak antiseptic solution or salt to prevent infection.
pg049_n0043: Then, cover it with a sterile gauze.
pg049_n0044: You can use plasters to cover minor cuts.
pg049_n0045: Assess the seriousness of the wound; if necessary, consult the doctor.
pg049_n0046: When using a knife, make sure that the sharp part is facing away from you.
pg049_n0047: When handling sharp knives, hold them by their handles and keep the handles free from grease or oil to avoid slipping off.
pg049_n0048: Keep all sharp and pointed utensils in a safe place.
pg049_n0049: Avoid washing knives together with other utensils.
pg050_n0003: Falling: A poor arrangement of kitchen equipment; wet walkways due to oil or water spills on the floor’s surface; poor disposal of kitchen refuse like peelings of bananas, tomatoes and fruits can cause falling in the kitchen.
pg050_n0004: In addition, inappropriate footwear, such as high-heeled shoes in the kitchen, can cause someone to fall.
pg050_n0006: To prevent falling, avoid storing frequently used items such as pots and pans on high shelves or cabinets.
pg050_n0007: Always keep the kitchen floor tidy; provide adequate lighting and wear appropriate shoes in the kitchen.
pg050_n0009: Electric shocks: These accidents happen in the kitchen when handling electric appliances with wet hands or when touching electric wire with an electrical current with bare feet or wet hands.
pg050_n0010: If an electric shock occurs, switch off the electrical current or main switch.
pg050_n0011: Use a poor conductor of electricity such as a wood stick to move a victim from the electricity; Then, seek medical assistance.
pg050_n0012: Never use wet materials to hold the victim.
pg050_n0014: To prevent an electric shock, never touch electrical instruments such as switches and sockets with wet hands as they can cause an accident.
pg050_n0015: Switch off all electrical appliances that are not in use.
pg050_n0016: Electrical wires should be well insulated.
pg050_n0017: Defective appliances should be repaired or replaced.

pg052_n0010: Fruits and vegetables are perishable foods.
pg052_n0011: They contain large amounts of water.
pg052_n0012: Therefore, they should be used immediately after harvesting to avoid spoilage.
pg052_n0013: They also contain essential vitamins, minerals and dietary fibre for promoting health.
pg052_n0014: In this chapter, you will learn about fruits and vegetables, types of fruits, classes of vegetables, and nutritive values of fruits and vegetables.
pg052_n0015: You will also learn about the storage of fruits and vegetables.
pg052_n0016: The competencies developed will enable you to use fruits and vegetables properly in order to improve your family’s health and income.
pg052_n0019: Food consumption without fruits and vegetables.
pg052_n0023: A fruit is a flesh, edible part of a plant.
pg052_n0024: It may or may not contain seeds.
pg052_n0025: It is typically sweet, sour or bitter.
pg052_n0026: Fruits can be eaten raw such as ripe bananas, oranges, mangoes and peaches or cooked to make various dishes.
pg052_n0027: For example, an apple is an ingredient for making apple charlotte, a pineapple is used to make pineapple upside down cake and a ripe banana is used to make banana fritters.
pg052_n0028: They can also be raw materials for making refreshing and nourishing beverages.
pg052_n0032: Fruits contain important nutrients needed by the body in the following ways:
pg052_n0035: Fruits contain numerous compounds for a healthy heart.
pg052_n0036: For example, apples, mangoes, ripe bananas, and oranges are rich in potassium, which helps to regulate blood pressure.
pg053_n0003: They boost body energy. Fruits contain sugar, which is digested and converted to energy. These fruits include ripe bananas, pineapples and watermelons. Fruits such as avocados contain healthy fats that also energise the body.
pg053_n0006: Oranges, ripe bananas, apples, peaches, plums and avocados control blood sugar by enhancing insulin sensitivity and improving glucose clearance from the blood, hence preventing type 2 diabetes.
pg053_n0008: They reduce the risk of cancer.
pg053_n0009: Fruits rich in vitamins and antioxidants play an important role in preventing and managing cancers, such as breast cancer and liver cancer.
pg053_n0010: Regular consumption of fruits such as tangerines and oranges can help prevent these cancers.
pg053_n0012: Fruits reduce the risk of developing kidney stones.
pg053_n0013: Citrus fruits such as oranges and lemons have large amounts of vitamin C, which helps to reduce the chances of developing kidney stones.
pg053_n0016: Mangoes, avocados, papayas and watermelons are good sources of vitamin A, which helps to maintain eye health.
pg053_n0019: Oranges, apricots, tangerines and grape fruits contain calcium.
pg053_n0020: These nutrients help to maintain healthy bones and teeth.
pg053_n0023: Most fruits contain fibres which aid in digestion, hence preventing constipation.
pg053_n0024: Eating whole fruits, including their edible skins, provides the body with dietary fibres.
pg053_n0027: Citrus fruits, strawberries and pineapples are excellent hair stimulants.
pg053_n0028: The vitamin C present in such fruits prevents hair loss and keeps hair shiny and healthy.
pg053_n0029: Consuming these fruits ensures healthy hair growth and keeps the hair lustrous and soft.
pg053_n0030: For instance, avocados have an impressive amount of vitamin E, which is good for hair health.
pg053_n0033: Vitamin C-rich fruits, such as oranges, pineapples and papayas, improve body immunity.
pg053_n0036: Fruits are low in calories; hence, consuming them has little effect on adding extra body weight.
pg054_n0005: Types of fruits include soft, hard, stone, citrus, berry, dry and miscellaneous fruits.
pg054_n0007: Soft fruits: These fruits are delicate and fragile, with a very short shelf life.
pg054_n0008: Examples are strawberries and raspberries, as Figure 4.1 illustrates.

pg054_im058: A pile of ripe red raspberries with a few green leaves.
pg054_n0016: Hard fruits: These fruits are easy to store, and they can be kept for a much longer time without spoiling than other fruits.
pg054_n0017: Guava, pears, lemons and apples are examples of hard fruits.

pg055_n0011: Citrus fruits: These fruits have juicy pulp inside their leathery skins.
pg055_n0012: They grow on trees, bushes or shrubs.
pg055_n0013: They include oranges, grapefruits, tangerines, lemons and limes.

pg055_n0024: Berry fruits: These are small, fleshy fruits with numerous seeds.

pg055_im070: A pile of blueberries with green leaves on top.
pg055_n0034: Dry fruits: These fruits are normally eaten dry, such as baobab fruit and tamarind.
pg055_n0035: Others, such as sultanas and currants, can be dried through processing.

pg056_n0008: Miscellaneous fruits: These include fruits that are not classified elsewhere, such as watermelons, ripe bananas and pineapples.
pg056_n0009: These fruits are usually difficult to classify.
pg056_n0010: Watermelons and bananas are botanically classified as berries even though they have entirely different shapes.
pg056_n0011: Similarly, a pineapple is neither a pine nor an apple but a fruit consisting of many berries that have grown together.

pg057_n0005: The nutrient content of fruits varies considerably between varieties.
pg057_n0006: Except for avocados and guavas, most fruits have no protein or fat.
pg057_n0007: Their primary dietary contributions are carbohydrates, minerals, vitamins and water.
pg057_n0009: Carbohydrates: Fruits are an important part of a balanced meal as they provode energy without adding unnecessary calories.
pg057_n0010: Unripe fruits contain carbohydrates in the form of starch, ripe fruits contain carbohydrates in the form of sugar.
pg057_n0012: Minerals: Ripe bananas, oranges, apricots and grapefruits are rich in potassium and magnesium.
pg057_n0013: These nutrients are important in regulating blood pressure.
pg057_n0014: Apples, guavas and passion fruits contain small amounts of sodium, which is important for maintaining a proper water balance in the body.
pg057_n0015: Fruits such as strawberries and watermelons contain small amounts of iron, which enables blood formation.
pg057_n0016: Oranges, blackcurrants and blackberries contain easily absorbable calcium, which strengthens bones and teeth.
pg057_n0018: Vitamins: Strawberries, oranges, lemons and grapefruits contain vitamin C, which is a powerful antioxidant.
pg057_n0019: It helps in healing wounds and maintaining healthy skin.
pg057_n0020: Papayas contain folic acid, which is an essential nutrient for a pregnant woman as it facilitates the brain formation of the foetus and prevents the occurrence of spina bifida.
pg057_n0022: Water: Watermelons, apricots, strawberries, grapefruits, blueberries, oranges, peaches, papayas, pineapples and plums contain large amounts of water of up to 90 per cent.
pg057_n0023: The water present gives these fruits a refreshing quality.

pg058_n0022: Points to consider when selecting fruits
pg058_n0024: To select safe and quality fruits, you should consider the following tips:
pg058_n0029: Avoid overripe fruits since they may contain harmful bacteria.
pg058_n0030: Conversely, unripe fruits may be indigestible.
pg058_n0033: The skin of the fruit should be smooth without blemishes.
pg058_n0034: Citrus fruits must have fine skins.
pg058_n0037: Check the fruit’s colour to find out whether it is ripe.
pg058_n0038: For example, a ripe strawberry is deep red; a ripe banana is yellow; and a ripe orange is orange, as its name implies.
pg058_n0039: A cut watermelon has a deep red colour; when selecting a whole watermelon, it should be firm.
pg058_n0040: Ripe watermelons sound hollow when slapped.
pg058_n0043: Dried fruits should look fresh and dry, without stalks.
pg058_n0044: They should neither be shrivelled nor wrinkled.
pg058_n0047: Press the fruit to check its firmness.
pg058_n0048: For instance, apples should be firm.
pg058_n0051: Pay attention to the smell of the fruit.
pg058_n0052: A ripe fruit’s smell is easily noticeable even without smelling it up close; for instance, a ripe pineapple has a sweet smell, especially near the stem.
pg058_n0056: Fruits such as pears should be a bit softer around the stalk than others.
pg058_n0060: Certain fruits such as cherries and apples should have a waxy, shiny appearance.

pg059_n0020: Consider the following points when preparing fruits for consumption.
pg059_n0026: Germs on the peel or skin can get inside the fruits during cutting.
pg059_n0027: Wash the fruits even if you do not plan to eat their peels.
pg059_n0028: Do not wash fruits with soap, detergent or commercial produce, since it may introduce residues that may affect the consumer’s health.
pg059_n0032: Remove the stalk from the fruit.
pg059_n0033: Then, clean the fruit well using clean safe water.
pg059_n0034: Dry it well to remove any bacteria that may be present.
pg059_n0038: Use a clean sharp knife for peeling.
pg059_n0043: To retain vitamin C content, slice or cut the fruit and serve it immediately.

pg060_n0006: Thus, they should be stored well to avoid spoilage.
pg060_n0007: Appropriate fruit storage prevents contamination and nutrient loss.
pg060_n0008: Store fruits carefully to avoid crushing or bruising to prevent them from spoilage.
pg060_n0009: Fresh fruits should be stored in a clean, cool and well-ventilated place.
pg060_n0010: Do not keep fruits in very hot or cold places to increase their shelf life.
pg060_n0011: Moreover, do not pile up fruits, since they will produce ethylene gas, which speeds up the ripening process and causes spoilage.
pg060_n0012: Soft fruits are also best kept in the refrigerator as they deteriorate rapidly in warm conditions.
pg060_n0013: When storing fruits in the refrigerator, pack them in polythene bags to reduce dehydration and prevent other foods from absorbing their flavour.
pg060_n0014: Furthermore, do not store bananas in the refrigerator, because they will turn black.
pg060_n0015: If you do not have a refrigerator, do not store ripe fruits for more than two days, depending on their variety; mould, yeast and oxidation will spoil them.

pg064_n0016: Vegetables are edible parts of some plants including flowers, fruits, stems, leaves, roots and seeds.
pg064_n0017: They can be eaten raw or cooked.
pg064_n0018: They are grouped into leafy and non-leafy vegetables.
pg064_n0019: Vegetables can be served with the main meal or be part of the main meal.
pg064_n0020: Combining vegetables can also add good colour, texture and flavour to the food.
pg064_n0021: For example, preparing a mixed vegetable soup requires one to blend onions, carrots, tomatoes and cabbage to obtain nice coloured, textured and flavoured soup.
pg064_n0022: Carrots, tomatoes and lettuce leaves can also serve the purpose of garnishing the food before serving.
pg064_n0023: Most vegetables are rich sources of vitamins and minerals.
pg064_n0024: They also provide fibre, which aids in digestion.
pg065_n0007: Vegetables offer the following health benefits to the human body:
pg065_n0011: Vegetables are rich sources of micronutrients such as vitamins and minerals.
pg065_n0012: The vitamins found in most vegetables include vitamins A, B and C.
pg065_n0013: The minerals found in vegetables include iron, magnesium and zinc.
pg065_n0016: Vegetables contain antioxidants such as carotenoids.
pg065_n0017: These antioxidants protect the body against chronic diseases such as cancer.
pg065_n0020: Vegetables are low in fat but high in fibre; hence, consuming them reduces the risk of overweight, obesity, cardiovascular disease and diabetes.
pg065_n0023: Fibre in vegetables helps to absorb water and expands as it passes through the digestive system.
pg065_n0024: This process facilitates bowel movement and prevents constipation.

pg069_n0011: The level of nutrients in vegetables depends on vegetable variety, soil type, post-harvest handling and storage.

pg069_n0014: Water: Vegetables such as cabbage, tomatoes and cucumbers have high water contents, ranging from 90 to 95 per cent depending on the variety.
pg069_n0016: Vitamins: Vegetables are good sources of vitamins.
pg069_n0017: Tomatoes, carrots and leafy vegetables such as spinach and amaranth contain vitamin A.
pg069_n0018: Vegetable seeds contain some B vitamins.

pg069_n0022: Vitamin E is found in small amounts in green vegetables.
pg069_n0023: Vitamin K is found in green vegetables and green peas.
pg069_n0025: Minerals: Vegetables are a good source of minerals such as potassium, calcium, sulphur, magnesium, phosphate and iron.
pg069_n0026: For instance, cabbage contains high levels of calcium and phosphorous.
pg069_n0027: Spinach, green peas and green beans are good sources of iron.
pg069_n0028: Green vegetables also contain calcium and sulphur.
pg069_n0030: Protein: Vegetables such as green peas, green pigeon peas and mushrooms are good sources of vegetable protein.
pg069_n0032: Carbohydrates: Some vegetables contain carbohydrates in the form of starch and sugar.
pg069_n0033: Examples of these vegetables are beetroots, potatoes, onions, tomatoes and leeks.
pg069_n0035: Fat: Most vegetables contain insignificant amounts of fat.

pg072_n0032: Common methods of cooking vegetables include boiling, braising, stewing, frying and steaming.
pg072_n0033: Choose a method that will retain as many nutrients as possible.
pg072_n0035: Boiling: This is the simplest and the most common method of cooking food, including vegetables.
pg072_n0036: It involves submerging food in the boiling water or other liquids and cooking it until it becomes tender and fully cooked.
pg072_n0037: Boiling is used for a wide range of foods including vegetables such as green peas, carrots, broccoli, eggplants and French beans.
pg072_n0038: When boiling, cover the pot to prevent water vapour from escaping, thus retaining nutrients and enabling the temperature to rise more quickly so that the food boils fast.
pg072_n0039: Covering the pot helps in retaining nutrients.
pg072_n0040: Observe the following rules during boiling:
pg072_n0043: (i) Use moderate water to boil vegetables such as carrots, broccoli and eggplants to retain their flavour.
pg072_n0044: Too much water on vegetables leads to a less flavourful end product.
pg073_n0006: Avoid overcooking to retain shape, nutrients, colour and flavour.
pg073_n0009: Use the liquid obtained from boiling vegetables (stock) to make other foods such as soup and sauces.
pg073_n0012: Chop the vegetables into equal sizes to allow even cooking.
pg073_n0015: Once the water reaches a boiling point, reduce the heat to a gentle simmer.
pg073_n0016: Simmering ensures even cooking and prevents food from becoming too soft.
pg073_n0019: Start with cold water in the pot and bring the water to a boil before adding the food.
pg073_n0020: When water boils it ensures even cooking.
pg073_n0021: Advantages of the boiling cooking method
pg073_n0023: The boiling method offers several advantages, making it a popular and practical cooking technique for various ingredients.
pg073_n0024: The following are the advantages of the boiling method:
pg073_n0028: The liquid remaining after boiling some foods can be used to prepare soup, sauces and gravies; therefore, the dissolved nutrients are not lost.
pg073_n0031: It is possible to boil several types of food together (such as pumpkin and potatoes).
pg073_n0032: Hence, the process saves both fuel and time.
pg073_n0035: It is a simple and quick method of cooking, depending on the type of vegetable to be cooked.
pg073_n0044: While the boiling method offers many advantages, it also has disadvantages, which should be considered:
pg073_n0048: Boiling can cause water-soluble nutrients, such as B vitamins, vitamin C and minerals, to leach into the cooking water.
pg073_n0049: When this water is discarded, the nutrients are lost, reducing the food’s overall nutritional value.
pg073_n0052: Boiling food, especially vegetables and pulses, in large amounts of water, can dilute the natural flavours.
pg073_n0053: Their flavours may disperse into the cooking water, resulting in a less tasty end product.
pg074_n0004: (iii) It is easy to overcook food when boiling, especially when the cooking times are not carefully monitored.
pg074_n0005: Overcooked food can become mushy, unappetizing, and non- nutritious.
pg074_n0007: (iv) It can be costly due to fuel consumption; extended cooking consumes more energy than other cooking methods.
pg074_n0008: This can lead to higher utility bills.
pg074_n0010: (v) Boiling different foods in one pot can result in flavour transfer, where the flavours of one ingredient may be absorbed by another, altering the taste of the cooked dish.

pg074_n0021: Braising: This method involves a combination of the dry and moist heat cooking of vegetables.
pg074_n0022: Initially, one cooks vegetables in a small amount of oil before further simmering them in a small amount of water.
pg074_n0024: The vegetables cooked using this method are well-flavoured.
pg074_n0025: This method can be applied to celery, cabbage and onions.
pg074_n0029: Braising creates more tasty dishes as the food tends to have a richer taste because juices and flavours tend to seep in during braising.
pg074_n0033: Braising might spoil the texture of the food if carried out for a long time.
pg074_n0034: It also causes the leaching of nutrients in water such as vitamins B and C.
pg074_n0035: Prolonged braising can destroy nutrients such as vitamin C.
pg075_n0005: Stewing is a moist-heat cooking method that involves a slow and gentle cooking of food in a covered pot with a small amount of liquid.
pg075_n0006: This method is particularly suitable for cooking vegetables such as green peas, mushrooms, celery, leeks, mustard greens, eggplants, tomatoes, kale and peppers.
pg075_n0007: It makes the food tender and infused with delicious tastes of the cooking liquid.
pg075_n0011: To achieve delicious and well-cooked stews, follow these general rules:
pg075_n0015: Use a heavy-bottomed pot with a tight-fitting lid to ensure an even heat distribution and moisture retention during cooking.
pg075_n0018: Cut the food into uniform pieces to ensure even cooking.
pg075_n0021: Once the ingredients and liquid are mixed, bring the mixture to a boil; reduce the heat to a gentle simmer.
pg075_n0022: Cooking the stew slowly over low heat softens the ingredients and allows the flavour to blend together.
pg075_n0025: Add sufficient amount of liquid or stock to obtain enough stew.
pg075_n0028: Serve the food with the stew coming from cooking.
pg075_n0031: Always cook the stew in the covered pot to retain steam and maintain a consistent temperature.
pg075_n0032: This helps to tenderise the ingredients and prevents excessive evaporation.
pg075_n0035: Stir the stew occasionally to ensure even cooking and prevent sticking at the bottom.
pg075_n0038: If your stew includes both meat and vegetables, add the vegetables later in the cooking process to avoid overcooking them.
pg075_n0039: You may add dense vegetables such as carrots and potatoes at the beginning and more delicate vegetables such as peas and leaf vegetables towards the end.
pg075_n0045: Stewing is an economical method of cooking since it uses little fuel.
pg075_n0048: Stews do not require much attention during cooking as they need only a small amount of heat during cooking.
pg075_n0051: Nutrients are not lost because the stock is retained as part of the stew.
pg075_n0052: While some water-soluble nutrients may leach into the cooking liquid, stewing preserves significant amount of vitamins and minerals in the ingredients.
pg075_n0053: This makes the stew a nutritious and wholesome meal.
pg076_n0005: Stewing is a versatile cooking method one can use for a wide range of ingredients, including a variety of vegetables.
pg076_n0006: It allows for the combination of different flavours and textures in one pot.
pg076_n0009: Once the ingredients are added to the pot and brought to a simmer, stewing requires minimal hands-on time.
pg076_n0010: This makes it a convenient cooking method, especially for busy cooks.
pg076_n0013: Stewing is ideal for cooking in large batches, making it suitable for feeding a crowd.
pg076_n0016: Stews can be easily frozen and reheated, making them a convenient option for making ahead meals.
pg076_n0019: Stewing reduces food waste since it is an excellent way to use up leftover vegetables and meats.
pg076_n0023: While stewing food offers many advantages, it also has some disadvantages that should be considered:
pg076_n0027: This method is time-consuming, stewing is a slow-cooking method, and, depending on the ingredients, it can take a significant amount of time to achieve the desired tenderness and flavour.
pg076_n0030: The long cooking time can make the food soft or mushy.
pg076_n0031: Delicate vegetables may lose their crisp texture and vibrant colours when stewed for an extended period.
pg076_n0034: Although stewing retains more nutrients than is the case with other cooking methods water-soluble vitamins and minerals can still leach into the cooking liquid.
pg076_n0035: If the liquid is discarded or not consumed with the stew, some nutrients may be lost.
pg076_n0038: If not carefully monitored, stewing can lead to overcooking, resulting in a loss of flavour and texture.
pg076_n0039: Vegetables can become mushy and lose their nutritional value.
pg076_n0042: Once the ingredients are combined in the stew, it can be challenging to adjust the seasoning without overcooking the food.
pg076_n0043: It is essential to season the stew correctly from the beginning.
pg076_n0046: Stewing may not be suitable for certain ingredients that require high heat or quick cooking to retain their best qualities; for example, some leafy green vegetables may not cook well in a stew.

pg077_n0013: Frying: Frying is a method of cooking food in hot fat or oil.
pg077_n0014: This quick, convenient and popular method of cooking involves using a high temperature.
pg077_n0015: This method is divided into dry frying, shallow frying and deep frying.
pg077_n0016: Vegetables use shallow and deep frying methods.
pg077_n0020: Shallow frying involves cooking food using a small amount of oil in a shallow pan.
pg077_n0021: For example, eggplant and cauliflower can be fried using this method.
pg077_n0024: Deep frying involves cooking by completely immersing the food in hot oil.
pg077_n0025: Examples of deep-fried foods include fried vegetable samosas, and potato chips.
pg077_n0026: Observe the following rules when frying food
pg077_n0030: Heat the oil to the right temperature.
pg077_n0033: Put the food item into the oil carefully to avoid spilling.
pg077_n0036: Use fresh and clean fat and oil.
pg077_n0039: Thoroughly drain foods that are to be fried, such as potato chips, before frying them.
pg077_n0042: For deep frying, the oil should be two-thirds of the pan to avoid overflowing.
pg077_n0045: You can coat deep-fried foods such as kachori to prevent breakage.
pg077_n0048: Do not overfill the food in a pan to provide enough spacing for proper cooking.
pg078_n0007: The flavour of food is retained and improved.
pg078_n0010: The food acquires a nice appetising brown colour.
pg078_n0016: It gives the food a distinct aroma.
pg078_n0022: High heat treatment can affect water-soluble vitamins, such as vitamin C.
pg078_n0025: Frying adds extra calories to the body due to oil absorption, contributing to weight gain.
pg078_n0027: Steaming: Steaming is a gentle and healthy cooking method that involves cooking food using steam from boiling water.
pg078_n0028: Vegetables that can be steamed include spinach, broccoli, and other leafy greens such as carrots, cauliflower, green beans and asparagus.
pg078_n0029: Steaming methods include plate steaming, bowl steaming, colander steaming and steaming using food steamer.
pg078_n0033: The following rules should be observed during steaming:
pg078_n0037: The water used should be in a boiling state before you put food in the steamer.
pg078_n0040: The instructions given by the manufacturer should be followed when steaming vegetables using a food steamer.
pg078_n0043: Steam must be produced constantly during cooking.
pg078_n0046: To maintain the water temperature, boiling water should be added when needed.
pg078_n0049: The steamer or a pan must have a tight-fitting lid to avoid loss of steam.
pg078_n0050: The colander and plate should fit well on the saucepan.
pg078_n0053: When opening the lid, direct the steam away from you to avoid getting scalds.
pg079_n0004: Advantages of the steaming cooking method
pg079_n0009: Nutrient loss is reduced since the food does not get in contact with the cooking water directly.
pg079_n0013: Steaming allows food to retain its natural flavours, colours, and textures.
pg079_n0014: It does not require fats or oils, hence retaining the original taste of the ingredients.
pg079_n0018: Steaming is a low-fat cooking method since it does not require the addition of fat or oils.
pg079_n0019: This makes it an excellent choice for those who reduce their fat intake.
pg079_n0023: Steaming is a straightforward cooking technique that requires minimal preparation and clean up.
pg079_n0024: Once you have set up the steamer and put the food, it requires little attention, allowing you to focus on other meal preparations.
pg079_n0028: Steaming can be used for a wide range of ingredients, including vegetables, seafood, poultry, and even desserts like puddings.
pg079_n0029: It is a versatile cooking method that can be adapted to various food types.
pg079_n0033: Steaming provides even and gentle heat distribution, ensuring that the food cooks uniformly.
pg079_n0034: There is no risk of uneven cooking or burnt spots, as long as you follow the appropriate cooking time.
pg079_n0038: Steaming helps the food to retain its moisture, hence preventing it from drying out.
pg079_n0039: This is particularly beneficial for delicate ingredients such as fish or seafood that can easily become overcooked and dry with other cooking methods.
pg079_n0043: Since steaming typically involves using a steamer basket or rack, there are fewer pots and pans to clean compared to other cooking techniques.
pg079_n0047: Foods cooked by steaming are light and easy to digest; therefore, it is a suitable cooking method for invalids and convalescents.
pg079_n0049: Disadvantages of the steaming cooking method
pg079_n0054: Extended cooking time: Steaming, especially for larger or thicker ingredients, can take longer than is the case with other cooking methods, such as boiling or frying.
pg079_n0055: While steaming is gentle and preserves nutrients, it may not be the best option when you need to cook something quickly.
pg079_n0059: A steamer can cause scalds if carelessly handled.
pg080_n0007: Constant attention is required to ensure that the water is continuously boiling and replenished as required.
pg080_n0011: While steaming can be done using basic kitchen tools like a steamer basket or improvised setups, some people may prefer dedicated steamers (electric or stovetop), which can be an additional cost.
pg080_n0014: Steaming may not add significant flavour to cooked food, unlike roasting or grilling, which impart a smoky flavour.
pg080_n0017: Steamed dishes may lack the crispiness or textural variety found in dishes prepared using other methods, such as frying and baking.
pg080_n0020: Care must be taken not to overcook delicate ingredients, as steaming can quickly turn them mushy and negatively affect their appearance and taste.

pg082_n0019: Roasting is a method which involves cooking food in an oven or an open fire.
pg082_n0020: It is a dry cooking technique.
pg082_n0021: It can be done at low, moderate or high temperatures, depending on the food to be roasted.

pg083_n0009: The cook should observe the following rules when roasting food:
pg083_n0013: The oven and other heat sources should be pre-heated to the right temperature before putting the food item.
pg083_n0014: Preheating ensures even cooking and helps to achieve the desired texture and colour.
pg083_n0017: Leave the roasted food for a few minutes after removing it from the oven.
pg083_n0018: This period allows the juice to be redistributed, resulting in a more flavourful and tender dish.
pg083_n0020: Advantages of the roasting method of cooking
pg083_n0024: Roasting brings out the natural flavours of ingredients, making the food more tasty.
pg083_n0027: Roasting creates a crispy and golden exterior on vegetables such as potatoes.
pg083_n0030: Roasting requires little or no added fats or oils.
pg083_n0031: The high heat in the oven allows the food to cook in its juices, reducing the need for added fats while keeping the dish moist and tasty.
pg083_n0034: Oven roasting is a relatively simple cooking method.
pg083_n0035: Once the food is seasoned and put in the oven, it requires minimal attention, allowing you to prepare other ingredients of the meal or attend to other tasks.
pg083_n0038: Roasting can be used for a wide variety of ingredients apart from vegetables such as meats, poultry, fruits, and even nuts.
pg083_n0039: This versatility allows you to create a diverse range of dishes using the same cooking technique.
pg083_n0042: When compared to frying or sautéing in oil, roasting is a healthier cooking method.
pg083_n0043: It retains the nutrients of the ingredients, and the minimal use of added fats makes it a good choice for people aspiring to reduce calorie intake.
pg083_n0046: Roasting allows you to create one-pan meals by combining different ingredients in a roasting pan.
pg083_n0047: This simplifies the cooking process, reduces the number of dishes to clean, and allows flavours to blend together.
pg083_n0050: Roasting pans and baking sheets are often easy to clean, especially if lined with parchment paper or foil.
pg084_n0005: Roasting can be used to cook larger quantities of food at once, making it ideal for batch cooking or meals preparation for multiple servings.
pg084_n0008: Roasted dishes including vegetables have an elegant and appetizing appearance, making them ideal for guests and special occasions.
pg084_n0010: Disadvantages of the roasting method of cooking
pg084_n0014: Roasting requires a longer cooking time; roasting is generally a slower cooking method than in the case with other techniques such as frying or grilling.
pg084_n0015: Depending on the size and type of food being roasted, it may take more time to achieve the desired results.
pg084_n0018: Achieving even cooking with roasting can be a challenge, particularly when roasting large or irregularly shaped pieces of vegetables.
pg084_n0019: Using a roasting rack or turning the food during cooking can address this problem.
pg084_n0022: Browning variability: While browning is one of the appealing aspects of roasting, it can also vary based on factors such as the food’s moisture content, sugar content, and proximity to the heat source.
pg084_n0023: Ensuring consistent browning requires attention and adjustments during cooking.
pg084_n0026: Roasting large quantities of food or multiple dishes simultaneously may require ample oven space.
pg084_n0027: A limited oven capacity can be a disadvantage when preparing meals for a large number of people.
pg084_n0030: Some delicate foods, such as soft or thinly sliced vegetables, may not be well-suited for roasting, as they can become overcooked or lose their shape.

pg085_n0034: Like fruits, vegetables are also perishable.
pg085_n0035: Therefore, use vegetables when they are fresh.
pg085_n0036: When vegetables are not for immediately consumption, store them properly to avoid spoilage by micro-organisms.

pg086_n0003: Points to consider when preparing vegetables for cooking
pg086_n0005: Consider the following points when preparing vegetables for cooking.
pg086_n0012: To avoid nutrient loss, use fresh vegetables or immediately after removing them from the refrigerator.
