pg044_n0005_easy_read: Kitchen hygiene is important. It helps keep food safe and stops infectious diseases from spreading.
pg044_n0006_easy_read: Good kitchen hygiene helps people prepare and handle food safely. This lowers the risk of food contamination and the growth of harmful micro-organisms.
pg044_n0007_easy_read: So, think about kitchen hygiene, personal hygiene and food hygiene when you prepare, cook and serve food.
pg044_n0009_easy_read:
Kitchen hygiene:
This means keeping kitchen surfaces and equipment clean. It also means throwing away kitchen waste properly to avoid food contamination.
pg044_n0010_easy_read: A dirty kitchen smells unpleasant. It also helps germs and pests grow and multiply. Germs and pests are dangerous to health. They cause diseases.
pg044_n0011_easy_read: A dirty kitchen may cause falls. This can happen when water, oil or food spills on the kitchen floor.
pg044_n0012_easy_read: To keep the kitchen clean and hygienic, follow these rules:
pg044_n0016_easy_read: Make sure the kitchen has good ventilation. This helps avoid bad smells and pests.
pg044_n0019_easy_read: Wash all utensils straight after use. Then dry them properly.
pg044_n0022_easy_read: Clean all areas with soap and water when they are dirty. This includes work surfaces.
pg044_n0025_easy_read: Sweep and mop the floor often because the kitchen floor gets greasy and dirty.
pg044_n0028_easy_read: Wash kitchen cloths often with soap and warm water. Dry them in the sun. Iron them to kill germs.
pg044_n0031_easy_read: Check the kitchen often for plumbing leaks. This helps make sure water drains properly.
pg044_n0034_easy_read: Wrap all waste before you put it in the bin.
pg044_n0037_easy_read: Use a covered waste bin for kitchen waste.
pg044_n0038_easy_read: Empty the bin regularly to prevent odours and pests.
pg044_n0039_easy_read: Clean and disinfect the waste bin sometimes.
pg044_n0041_easy_read:
Food hygiene:
Food hygiene means the conditions and actions that make food safe to eat. Prepare, cook and store food properly to avoid contamination and poisoning.
Points to consider in food hygiene:
pg044_n0045_easy_read: Cover or wrap food well before you store it in a cool, suitable place. This helps stop it attracting pests and pets.
pg044_n0046_easy_read: Household pets carry micro-organisms. These may contaminate food in the kitchen.
pg044_n0049_easy_read: Use separate cutting boards for raw food and cooked food, such as meat, poultry and vegetables. This helps avoid cross-contamination.
pg045_n0006_easy_read:
Wash cooking pots and serving dishes with warm water and soap.
Then rinse them with running water.
pg045_n0009_easy_read:
Do not leave perishable foods at room temperature for a long time.
They can lose moisture and attract microorganisms that spoil food.
pg045_n0012_easy_read:
Store different foods in the right places.
This helps stop spoilage and bad smells in the kitchen.
pg045_n0015_easy_read:
Keep raw foods away from ready-to-eat foods.
This helps prevent cross-contamination.
pg045_n0018_easy_read: Cook all foods that need cooking well.
pg045_n0021_easy_read:
Thaw frozen food before cooking.
This helps heat go all the way through the food.
pg045_n0024_easy_read: Use clean and safe water to cook food.
pg045_n0027_easy_read: Keep food at the right temperature to stop spoilage.
pg045_n0030_easy_read:
Wash fruits and vegetables well with clean and safe running water.
This is especially important for fruits and vegetables that people eat raw.
pg045_n0033_easy_read:
Personal hygiene in the kitchen is important.
It helps keep food safe and prevents food contamination and poisoning.
pg045_n0034_easy_read: Food handlers should follow these hygiene rules:
pg045_n0038_easy_read: Wash your hands well with soap and clean water before handling food and after using the toilet.
pg045_n0041_easy_read:
Do not touch your clothes, nose, mouth, hair, or other body parts when preparing food.
Bacteria can get onto the food.
pg045_n0042_easy_read: Always cover your mouth and nose with a handkerchief when you cough or sneeze.
pg045_n0045_easy_read:
Remove jewellery such as rings and watches before handling food.
This helps stop bacteria getting trapped.
pg045_n0048_easy_read:
Wear protective clothing such as an apron to avoid getting dirty.
Cover your hair with a hat or head scarf.
This helps stop micro-organisms from contaminating food.
pg045_n0051_easy_read:
Keep your fingernails short.
Long nails can carry microorganisms.
pg045_n0054_easy_read: Cover cuts, sores, or wounds with clean, sterile, waterproof bandages while preparing and cooking food.
pg046_n0003_easy_read:
(g)
Wear shoes in the kitchen.
This helps protect your body from accidents, such as falling.
pg046_n0004_easy_read: Wearing shoes also helps protect you from bacteria and food particles in the kitchen.
pg046_n0006_easy_read:
(h)
People with infections such as diarrhoea, typhoid, and cholera should not handle food.

It is necessary to practise good safety measures in the kitchen.
This helps prevent or stop accidents and illnesses.
These can lead to pain, discomfort, and death.
pg046_n0035_easy_read:
You should take safety precautions when doing different activities in the kitchen.
This helps prevent possible accidents.
pg046_n0036_easy_read: Table 3.1 shows some causes of accidents in the kitchen and the safety precautions to follow.
pg047_n0013_easy_read: Kitchen equipment, such as knives and cookers
pg047_n0016_easy_read: (i) When you use sharp knives, always cut away from your body.
pg047_n0017_easy_read: (ii) Always use a chopping board. This helps lower the risk of cutting your hand.
pg047_n0018_easy_read: (iii) Store knives out of the reach of children. Make sure the sharp blades point down.
pg047_n0023_easy_read: (i) Turn off burners and hot plates after use.
pg047_n0024_easy_read: (ii) Use oven gloves to take food out of the oven.
pg047_n0025_easy_read: (iii) Turn the pan's handle inwards during cooking.

pg048_n0040_easy_read: The kitchen can be a place with many dangers and accidents if people do not follow proper safety measures.
pg048_n0041_easy_read:
These accidents commonly happen in the kitchen:
- burns
- scalds
- fires
- cuts
pg048_n0043_easy_read: Burns: Burns can happen when a person touches hot surfaces, such as pots, pans, and cookers, or hot liquids such as oil.
pg048_n0044_easy_read:
For example, a pan of oil can get too hot and catch fire.
This can burn the person who tries to put out the fire.
pg048_n0045_easy_read: To avoid burns, use pot holders to
pg049_n0006_easy_read: Also, use oven gloves to pull out oven racks when you take dishes out after cooking.
pg049_n0008_easy_read: If you get a burn, cool the whole area with cold water for several minutes. This helps reduce pain and lowers the risk of blisters.
pg049_n0009_easy_read: If blisters appear, do not break them.
pg049_n0010_easy_read: Apply some petroleum jelly. Keep the burnt area away from the air because air will cause more pain.
pg049_n0011_easy_read: You can cover minor burns with sterile gauze and bandages.
pg049_n0014_easy_read: Scalds happen when hot liquid burns you, such as hot water or steam.
pg049_n0015_easy_read: For example, hot steam from food can also cause scalds.
pg049_n0016_easy_read: To prevent scalds, keep boiling pots steady. Turn the handles away from the cooker.
pg049_n0017_easy_read: Use pot holders when you remove pans or pots from the cooker.
pg049_n0018_easy_read: When you open lids while cooking, direct the steam away from you.
pg049_n0019_easy_read: If scalds happen, dip the injured part in cold water.
pg049_n0020_easy_read: This will cool the body and reduce the pain.
pg049_n0021_easy_read: Do not break the blisters. They protect the injured part from bacterial infection.
pg049_n0022_easy_read: Apply petroleum jelly on the scalds.
pg049_n0025_easy_read: A fire in the kitchen can start because of a gas pipe leak. It can also start when the cooker touches things that catch fire, like curtains or kitchen cloths.
pg049_n0026_easy_read: Turning the cooker on by accident, or leaving it on, can also cause a fire.
pg049_n0027_easy_read: To reduce this risk, always unplug electrical appliances or turn off cooking stoves after use.
pg049_n0028_easy_read: Never pour water on a grease fire.
pg049_n0029_easy_read: Instead, use a large pan lid to stop the fire from spreading.
pg049_n0030_easy_read: You can also put a damp towel over the fire to put it out.
pg049_n0031_easy_read: If you smell gas, turn off all gas jets and open the windows. This helps clear any gas that has built up.
pg049_n0032_easy_read: When you light the gas cooker, light the match first. Then turn on the gas.
pg049_n0033_easy_read: Do not keep anything near the cooker that may attract children, such as snacks.
pg049_n0034_easy_read:
Keep all items away from the cooker, such as:
- kitchen cloths
- curtains
pg049_n0035_easy_read: It is good to keep a fire extinguisher ready to use. But do not use it on a grease fire, because it can spread the burning grease around the kitchen.
pg049_n0036_easy_read: Keep children and pets away from cooking areas. This helps reduce the risk of accidents that could lead to fire.
pg049_n0039_easy_read: Chop or cut food carefully. This helps you avoid cutting your hand and causing injuries.
pg049_n0040_easy_read: Do not wash knives and sharp objects together with other utensils.
pg049_n0041_easy_read: Broken glass in the kitchen can also cause cuts.
pg049_n0042_easy_read: If you get a cut, clean the wound with a weak antiseptic solution or salt. This helps prevent infection.
pg049_n0043_easy_read: Then cover the wound with sterile gauze.
pg049_n0044_easy_read: You can use plasters to cover minor cuts.
pg049_n0045_easy_read: Check how serious the wound is. If needed, see a doctor.
pg049_n0046_easy_read: When you use a knife, make sure the sharp part faces away from you.
pg049_n0047_easy_read: When you handle sharp knives, hold them by the handles. Keep the handles free from grease or oil so they do not slip.
pg049_n0048_easy_read: Keep all sharp and pointed utensils in a safe place.
pg049_n0049_easy_read: Do not wash knives together with other utensils.
pg050_n0003_easy_read:
Falling: These things can cause falls in the kitchen:
- kitchen equipment placed badly
- wet walkways from oil or water spilled on the floor
- kitchen waste thrown away badly, such as banana peel, tomato peel, and fruit peel
pg050_n0004_easy_read:
Also, unsuitable shoes can make someone fall in the kitchen.
For example, high-heeled shoes can cause a fall.
pg050_n0006_easy_read: To prevent falls, do not keep things you use often, such as pots and pans, on high shelves or in high cupboards.
pg050_n0007_easy_read:
Always keep the kitchen floor tidy.
Make sure the kitchen has enough light.
Wear suitable shoes in the kitchen.
pg050_n0009_easy_read: Electric shocks: These accidents happen in the kitchen when someone uses electrical appliances with wet hands, or touches a live electric wire with bare feet or wet hands.
pg050_n0010_easy_read: If an electric shock happens, switch off the electricity or the main switch.
pg050_n0011_easy_read:
Use something that does not carry electricity well, such as a wooden stick, to move the victim away from the electricity.
Then get medical help.
pg050_n0012_easy_read: Never use wet materials to hold the victim.
pg050_n0014_easy_read:
To prevent an electric shock, never touch electrical items such as switches and sockets with wet hands.
They can cause an accident.
pg050_n0015_easy_read: Switch off all electrical appliances that you are not using.
pg050_n0016_easy_read: Electrical wires should have good insulation.
pg050_n0017_easy_read: Broken electrical appliances should be repaired or replaced.

pg052_n0012_easy_read: So, people should use fruits and vegetables soon after harvesting to stop them from spoiling.
pg052_n0013_easy_read: Fruits and vegetables also contain important vitamins, minerals and dietary fibre. These help to keep people healthy.

pg052_n0023_easy_read: A fruit is the fleshy, edible part of a plant.
pg052_n0024_easy_read: A fruit may contain seeds, or it may not contain seeds.
pg052_n0025_easy_read: A fruit is usually sweet, sour or bitter.
pg052_n0026_easy_read:
People can eat fruits raw, such as:
- ripe bananas
- oranges
- mangoes
- peaches
People can also cook fruits to make different dishes.
pg052_n0027_easy_read:
For example:
- people use apple to make apple charlotte
- people use pineapple to make pineapple upside down cake
- people use ripe banana to make banana fritters
pg052_n0028_easy_read: Fruits can also be used to make refreshing and nourishing drinks.
pg052_n0032_easy_read: Fruits contain important nutrients that the body needs in these ways:
pg052_n0035_easy_read: Fruits contain many substances that help to keep the heart healthy.
pg052_n0036_easy_read: For example, apples, mangoes, ripe bananas and oranges are rich in potassium. Potassium helps to regulate blood pressure.
pg053_n0003_easy_read:
Fruits give the body energy.
Fruits contain sugar. The body digests this sugar and turns it into energy.
These fruits include:
- ripe bananas
- pineapples
- watermelons
Avocados contain healthy fats. These fats also give the body energy.
pg053_n0006_easy_read:
These fruits help control blood sugar:
- oranges
- ripe bananas
- apples
- peaches
- plums
- avocados
They do this by improving insulin sensitivity and helping the blood clear glucose. This helps prevent type 2 diabetes.
pg053_n0008_easy_read: Fruits reduce the risk of cancer.
pg053_n0009_easy_read:
Fruits that are rich in vitamins and antioxidants help prevent and manage some cancers, such as:
- breast cancer
- liver cancer
pg053_n0010_easy_read: Eating fruits such as tangerines and oranges regularly can help prevent these cancers.
pg053_n0012_easy_read: Fruits reduce the risk of kidney stones.
pg053_n0013_easy_read: Citrus fruits such as oranges and lemons contain a lot of vitamin C. Vitamin C helps reduce the chance of getting kidney stones.
pg053_n0015_easy_read: Fruits help keep the eyes healthy.
pg053_n0016_easy_read:
These fruits are good sources of vitamin A:
- mangoes
- avocados
- papayas
- watermelons
Vitamin A helps keep the eyes healthy.
pg053_n0018_easy_read: Fruits help keep bones and teeth strong.
pg053_n0019_easy_read:
These fruits contain calcium:
- oranges
- apricots
- tangerines
- grape fruits
pg053_n0020_easy_read: These nutrients help keep bones and teeth healthy.
pg053_n0023_easy_read: Most fruits contain fibre. Fibre helps digestion and helps prevent constipation.
pg053_n0024_easy_read: Eating whole fruits, including the skins you can eat, gives the body dietary fibre.
pg053_n0027_easy_read:
These fruits are excellent hair stimulants:
- citrus fruits
- strawberries
- pineapples
pg053_n0028_easy_read: The vitamin C in these fruits prevents hair loss. It also keeps hair shiny and healthy.
pg053_n0029_easy_read: Eating these fruits helps hair grow well. It also keeps hair shiny and soft.
pg053_n0030_easy_read: For example, avocados contain a large amount of vitamin E. Vitamin E is good for hair health.
pg053_n0033_easy_read:
Fruits rich in vitamin C improve body immunity, such as:
- oranges
- pineapples
- papayas
pg053_n0036_easy_read: Fruits are low in calories. So, eating them has little effect on extra body weight.
pg054_n0005_easy_read:
Types of fruits include:
- soft fruits
- hard fruits
- stone fruits
- citrus fruits
- berry fruits
- dry fruits
- miscellaneous fruits
pg054_n0007_easy_read:
Soft fruits: These fruits are delicate and fragile.
They do not stay fresh for long.
pg054_n0008_easy_read: Examples are strawberries and raspberries, as Figure 4.1 shows.
pg054_n0016_easy_read:
Hard fruits: These fruits are easy to store.
They can stay good for much longer than other fruits.
pg054_n0017_easy_read:
Examples of hard fruits are:
- guava
- pears
- lemons
- apples
pg054_n0028_easy_read: Stone fruits: These fruits have flesh or pulp around a stone.
pg054_n0029_easy_read:
Examples are:
- mangoes
- peaches
- plums
- grapes
Figure 4.3 shows these fruits.
pg055_n0011_easy_read: Citrus fruits: These fruits have juicy flesh inside thick skins.
pg055_n0012_easy_read: Citrus fruits grow on trees, bushes, or shrubs.
pg055_n0013_easy_read:
These fruits include:
- oranges
- grapefruits
- tangerines
- lemons
- limes
pg055_n0024_easy_read: Berry fruits: These are small, fleshy fruits with many seeds.
pg055_n0034_easy_read: Dry fruits: People usually eat these fruits dry, such as baobab fruit and tamarind.
pg055_n0035_easy_read: Other fruits, such as sultanas and currants, can be dried by processing.
pg056_n0008_easy_read:
Miscellaneous fruits:
These are fruits that are not classified elsewhere.
Examples are:
- watermelons
- ripe bananas
- pineapples
pg056_n0009_easy_read: These fruits are usually hard to classify.
pg056_n0010_easy_read: In botany, watermelons and bananas are classified as berries, even though their shapes are very different.
pg056_n0011_easy_read:
In the same way, a pineapple is not a pine or an apple.
It is a fruit made of many berries that have grown together.

pg057_n0006_easy_read:
Most fruits have no protein or fat.
Avocados and guavas are exceptions.
pg057_n0007_easy_read:
Fruits mainly give the diet:
- carbohydrates
- minerals
- vitamins
- water
pg057_n0009_easy_read:
Carbohydrates:
Fruits are an important part of a balanced meal.
They give energy without adding extra calories.
pg057_n0010_easy_read:
Unripe fruits contain carbohydrates as starch.
Ripe fruits contain carbohydrates as sugar.
pg057_n0012_easy_read:
Minerals:
Ripe bananas, oranges, apricots and grapefruits are rich in potassium and magnesium.
pg057_n0013_easy_read: Potassium and magnesium are important for controlling blood pressure.
pg057_n0014_easy_read:
Apples, guavas and passion fruits contain small amounts of sodium.
Sodium helps the body keep the right water balance.
pg057_n0015_easy_read:
Strawberries and watermelons contain small amounts of iron.
Iron helps the body make blood.
pg057_n0016_easy_read:
Oranges, blackcurrants and blackberries contain calcium that the body can absorb easily.
Calcium makes bones and teeth stronger.
pg057_n0018_easy_read:
Vitamins:
Strawberries, oranges, lemons and grapefruits contain vitamin C.
Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant.
pg057_n0019_easy_read:
Vitamin C helps wounds heal.
It also helps keep skin healthy.
pg057_n0020_easy_read:
Papayas contain folic acid.
This is an essential nutrient for a pregnant woman.
It helps the foetus's brain to form.
It also helps prevent spina bifida.
pg057_n0022_easy_read:
Water:
These fruits contain a lot of water, up to 90%:
- watermelons
- apricots
- strawberries
- grapefruits
- blueberries
- oranges
- peaches
- papayas
- pineapples
- plums
pg057_n0023_easy_read: The water in these fruits makes them refreshing.

pg058_n0024_easy_read: To choose safe, good-quality fruits, follow these tips:

pg060_n0007_easy_read: Storing fruits the right way prevents contamination and loss of nutrients.
pg060_n0008_easy_read:
Store fruits carefully.
This helps to stop crushing and bruising, which can make fruits spoil.
pg060_n0009_easy_read: Store fresh fruits in a clean, cool place with good air flow.
pg060_n0010_easy_read:
Do not keep fruits in places that are very hot or very cold.
This helps fruits last longer.
pg060_n0011_easy_read:
Do not pile fruits up.
Fruits produce ethylene gas.
This gas makes fruits ripen faster and spoil.
pg060_n0012_easy_read:
It is best to keep soft fruits in the refrigerator.
Soft fruits spoil quickly in warm places.
pg060_n0013_easy_read:
When you store fruits in the refrigerator, put them in polythene bags.
This helps to stop them drying out.
It also stops other foods from taking in their flavour.
pg060_n0014_easy_read: Do not store bananas in the refrigerator because they will turn black.
pg060_n0015_easy_read:
If you do not have a refrigerator, keep ripe fruits for no more than 2 days, depending on the type of fruit.
Mould, yeast and oxidation will spoil them.

Common methods of cooking vegetables are:
- boiling
- braising
- stewing

pg072_n0035_easy_read:
Boiling:
Boiling is the simplest and most common way to cook food, including vegetables.
pg072_n0036_easy_read: Boiling means putting food into boiling water or another liquid and cooking it until it is soft and fully cooked.
pg072_n0037_easy_read:
People use boiling for many foods, including these vegetables:
- green peas
- carrots
- broccoli
- eggplants
- French beans
pg072_n0038_easy_read:
When you boil food, cover the pot.
This stops water vapour from escaping.
It helps keep nutrients in the food.
It also helps the temperature rise faster, so the food boils quickly.
pg072_n0039_easy_read: Covering the pot helps keep nutrients in the food.
pg072_n0043_easy_read:
(i) Use a moderate amount of water when you boil vegetables such as carrots, broccoli and eggplants.
This helps keep their flavour.
pg072_n0044_easy_read: Too much water on vegetables makes the final food less flavourful.
pg073_n0006_easy_read: Do not overcook the food. This helps it keep its shape, nutrients, colour and flavour.
pg073_n0009_easy_read: Use the liquid from boiled vegetables, called stock, to make other foods such as soup and sauces.
pg073_n0012_easy_read: Chop the vegetables into equal sizes so they cook evenly.
pg073_n0015_easy_read: When the water starts to boil, turn the heat down to a gentle simmer.
pg073_n0016_easy_read: Simmering helps the food cook evenly. It also stops the food from becoming too soft.
pg073_n0019_easy_read: Start with cold water in the pot. Bring the water to the boil before you add the food.
pg073_n0020_easy_read: Boiling water helps the food cook evenly.
pg073_n0023_easy_read: Boiling has several advantages. This makes it a popular and practical way to cook different ingredients.
pg073_n0024_easy_read: These are the advantages of boiling:
pg073_n0028_easy_read:
The liquid left after boiling some foods can be used to make:
- soup
- sauces
- gravies

This means the dissolved nutrients are not lost.
pg073_n0031_easy_read: You can boil several types of food together, such as pumpkin and potatoes.
pg073_n0032_easy_read: This saves both fuel and time.
pg073_n0035_easy_read: This is a simple and quick way to cook. It depends on the type of vegetable.
pg073_n0044_easy_read: Boiling has many advantages. But it also has disadvantages that you should consider:
pg073_n0048_easy_read:
Boiling can make water-soluble nutrients go into the cooking water. These nutrients include:
- B vitamins
- vitamin C
- minerals
pg073_n0049_easy_read: If you throw this water away, the nutrients are lost. This reduces the food's nutritional value.
pg073_n0052_easy_read: Boiling food in a lot of water can weaken the natural flavours. This is especially true for vegetables and pulses.
pg073_n0053_easy_read: The flavours may go into the cooking water. This can make the final food less tasty.
pg074_n0004_easy_read: (iii) It is easy to cook food for too long when you boil it, especially if you do not watch the cooking time carefully.
pg074_n0005_easy_read:
Food that is cooked for too long can become:
- soft and mushy
- not pleasant to eat
- less nutritious
pg074_n0007_easy_read: (iv) Boiling can cost a lot because it uses fuel. Cooking for a long time uses more energy than other cooking methods.
pg074_n0008_easy_read: This can make your utility bills higher.
pg074_n0010_easy_read: (v) Boiling different foods in 1 pot can mix their flavours. The flavour of 1 food may go into another food. This can change the taste of the dish.

pg074_n0021_easy_read: Braising: This method uses both dry heat and moist heat to cook vegetables.
pg074_n0022_easy_read: First, cook the vegetables in a small amount of oil. Then simmer them in a small amount of water.
pg074_n0024_easy_read: Vegetables cooked in this way have a good flavour.
pg074_n0025_easy_read:
You can use this method for:
- celery

- onions
pg074_n0029_easy_read: Braising makes dishes tastier. The food often has a richer taste because juices and flavours soak in during braising.
pg074_n0033_easy_read: Braising can spoil the texture of the food if you do it for too long.
pg074_n0034_easy_read: It also causes some nutrients to go into the water, such as vitamins B and C.
pg074_n0035_easy_read: Braising for a long time can destroy nutrients such as vitamin C.
pg075_n0005_easy_read:
Stewing is a moist-heat cooking method.
You cook food slowly and gently in a covered pot with a small amount of liquid.
pg075_n0006_easy_read:
This method is good for cooking vegetables such as:
- green peas
- mushrooms
- celery
- leeks
- mustard greens
- eggplants
- tomatoes
- kale
- peppers
pg075_n0007_easy_read:
It makes the food soft.
It also gives the food the taste of the cooking liquid.
pg075_n0011_easy_read: To make tasty and well-cooked stew, follow these general rules:
pg075_n0015_easy_read:
Use a pot with a heavy bottom and a tight-fitting lid.
This helps the heat spread evenly and keeps moisture in during cooking.
pg075_n0018_easy_read:
Cut the food into pieces of the same size.
This helps the food cook evenly.
pg075_n0021_easy_read:
After you mix the ingredients and liquid, bring the mixture to the boil.
Then reduce the heat and let it simmer gently.
pg075_n0022_easy_read:
Cooking the stew slowly over low heat softens the ingredients.
It also lets the flavours blend together.
pg075_n0025_easy_read: Add enough liquid or stock to make enough stew.
pg075_n0028_easy_read: Serve the food with the stew from the cooking pot.
pg075_n0031_easy_read:
Always cook the stew in a covered pot.
This keeps in the steam and keeps the temperature steady.
pg075_n0032_easy_read:
This helps to soften the ingredients.
It also stops too much liquid from evaporating.
pg075_n0035_easy_read:
Stir the stew from time to time.
This helps it cook evenly and stops it sticking to the bottom.
pg075_n0038_easy_read:
If your stew has both meat and vegetables, add the vegetables later.
This stops them from overcooking.
pg075_n0039_easy_read:
You can add firm vegetables such as carrots and potatoes at the beginning.
Add delicate vegetables such as peas and leaf vegetables near the end.
pg075_n0045_easy_read: Stewing is a cheap cooking method because it uses little fuel.
pg075_n0048_easy_read:
Stews do not need much attention while they cook.
They need only a small amount of heat.
pg075_n0051_easy_read: The stew keeps its nutrients because the stock stays in the stew.
pg075_n0052_easy_read:
Some water-soluble nutrients may go into the cooking liquid.
But stewing still keeps a large amount of vitamins and minerals in the ingredients.
pg075_n0053_easy_read: This makes the stew a nutritious and wholesome meal.
pg076_n0005_easy_read: Stewing is a flexible cooking method. You can use it for many ingredients, including different vegetables.
pg076_n0006_easy_read: It lets you mix different flavours and textures in 1 pot.
pg076_n0009_easy_read: After you put the ingredients in the pot and bring them to a simmer, stewing needs very little work from you.
pg076_n0010_easy_read: This makes stewing a convenient cooking method, especially for busy cooks.
pg076_n0013_easy_read: Stewing is good for cooking large amounts of food. This makes it suitable for feeding many people.
pg076_n0016_easy_read: You can easily freeze stews and heat them again later. This makes them a convenient choice for meals you make ahead.
pg076_n0019_easy_read: Stewing reduces food waste because it is a good way to use leftover vegetables and meat.
pg076_n0023_easy_read: Stewing food has many advantages. But it also has some disadvantages to think about:
pg076_n0027_easy_read: This method takes a long time. Stewing is a slow cooking method. Depending on the ingredients, it can take a lot of time to get the tenderness and flavour you want.
pg076_n0030_easy_read: The long cooking time can make the food soft or mushy.
pg076_n0031_easy_read: Delicate vegetables can lose their crisp texture and bright colours if you stew them for a long time.
pg076_n0034_easy_read: Stewing keeps more nutrients than some other cooking methods. But water-soluble vitamins and minerals can still move into the cooking liquid.
pg076_n0035_easy_read: If you throw away the liquid, or do not eat it with the stew, some nutrients may be lost.
pg076_n0038_easy_read: If you do not watch stewing carefully, the food can overcook. This can cause a loss of flavour and texture.
pg076_n0039_easy_read: Vegetables can become mushy and lose their nutritional value.
pg076_n0042_easy_read: After you mix the ingredients into the stew, it can be hard to change the seasoning without overcooking the food.
pg076_n0043_easy_read: It is important to season the stew correctly from the start.
pg076_n0046_easy_read: Stewing may not suit some ingredients. Some ingredients need high heat or quick cooking to keep their best qualities. For example, some leafy green vegetables may not cook well in a stew.

pg077_n0013_easy_read: Frying: Frying is a way of cooking food in hot fat or oil.
pg077_n0014_easy_read:
This cooking method is quick, easy and popular.
It uses high heat.
pg077_n0015_easy_read:
This method has 3 types:
- dry frying
- shallow frying
- deep frying
pg077_n0016_easy_read: For vegetables, use shallow frying and deep frying methods.
pg077_n0020_easy_read: Shallow frying means cooking food in a small amount of oil in a shallow pan.
pg077_n0021_easy_read: For example, you can fry eggplant and cauliflower in this way.
pg077_n0024_easy_read: Deep frying means cooking food by putting it completely into hot oil.
pg077_n0025_easy_read: Examples of deep-fried foods are fried vegetable samosas and potato chips.
pg077_n0026_easy_read: Follow these rules when frying food:
pg077_n0030_easy_read: Heat the oil to the right temperature.
pg077_n0033_easy_read: Put the food into the oil carefully to avoid spills.
pg077_n0036_easy_read: Use fresh, clean fat and oil.

pg077_n0048_easy_read:

pg078_n0007_easy_read: The flavour of the food stays in the food and becomes better.

pg078_n0013_easy_read: It makes the cooking time shorter.
pg078_n0016_easy_read: It gives the food a clear smell.
pg078_n0022_easy_read: High heat can affect vitamins that dissolve in water, such as vitamin C.
pg078_n0025_easy_read: Frying adds extra calories because the food absorbs oil. This can lead to weight gain.

Steaming:
Steaming is a gentle and healthy way to cook food.
It cooks food with steam from boiling water.
pg078_n0028_easy_read:
Vegetables you can steam include:
- spinach
- broccoli
- carrots
- cauliflower
- green beans
- asparagus
- other leafy greens
pg078_n0029_easy_read:
Steaming methods include:
- plate steaming
- bowl steaming
- colander steaming
- steaming using a food steamer
pg078_n0037_easy_read: The water must be boiling before you put the food in the steamer.
pg078_n0040_easy_read: Follow the manufacturer's instructions when you steam vegetables in a food steamer.
pg078_n0043_easy_read: Steam must be produced all the time during cooking.
pg078_n0046_easy_read: Add boiling water when needed to keep the water at the right temperature.
pg078_n0049_easy_read: The steamer or pan must have a tight-fitting lid so steam does not escape.
pg078_n0050_easy_read: The colander and plate should fit well on the saucepan.
pg078_n0053_easy_read: When you open the lid, direct the steam away from you to avoid scalds.
pg079_n0009_easy_read: Food loses fewer nutrients because the food does not touch the cooking water directly.
pg079_n0013_easy_read: Steaming helps food keep its natural flavours, colours, and textures.
pg079_n0014_easy_read: Steaming does not need fats or oils. This helps the ingredients keep their original taste.
pg079_n0018_easy_read: Steaming is a low-fat way of cooking because it does not need added fat or oils.
pg079_n0019_easy_read: This makes steaming a very good choice for people who want to eat less fat.
pg079_n0023_easy_read: Steaming is a simple cooking method. It needs little preparation and little cleaning up.
pg079_n0024_easy_read: After you set up the steamer and put in the food, steaming needs little attention. This lets you focus on preparing other parts of the meal.
pg079_n0028_easy_read:
You can use steaming for many types of food, including:
- vegetables
- seafood
- poultry
- desserts such as puddings
pg079_n0029_easy_read: Steaming is a flexible cooking method. You can use it for different types of food.
pg079_n0033_easy_read: Steaming spreads heat evenly and gently. This helps the food cook evenly.
pg079_n0034_easy_read: There is no risk of uneven cooking or burnt spots if you use the correct cooking time.
pg079_n0038_easy_read: Steaming helps food keep its moisture. This stops the food from drying out.
pg079_n0039_easy_read: This is especially helpful for delicate foods such as fish or seafood. With other cooking methods, these foods can easily overcook and dry out.
pg079_n0043_easy_read: Steaming usually uses a steamer basket or rack. So there are fewer pots and pans to clean than with other cooking methods.
pg079_n0047_easy_read: Steamed food is light and easy to digest. So steaming is a suitable cooking method for invalids and convalescents.
pg079_n0054_easy_read: Longer cooking time: Steaming can take longer than other cooking methods, such as boiling or frying. This is especially true for larger or thicker foods.
pg079_n0055_easy_read: Steaming is gentle and helps keep nutrients. But it may not be the best choice when you need to cook food quickly.
pg079_n0059_easy_read: A steamer can cause scalds if you do not handle it carefully.
pg080_n0007_easy_read:
You must watch the water all the time.
Make sure it keeps boiling.
Add more water when needed.
pg080_n0011_easy_read:
You can steam food with simple kitchen tools, such as a steamer basket or a simple homemade setup.
Some people may prefer a special steamer, either electric or for the hob.
This can cost extra.
pg080_n0014_easy_read:
Steaming may not add much flavour to cooked food.
Roasting and grilling can add a smoky flavour.
pg080_n0017_easy_read:
Steamed dishes may not be crispy.
They may also have less variety in texture than food cooked in other ways, such as frying and baking.
pg080_n0020_easy_read:
Be careful not to cook delicate ingredients for too long.
Steaming can quickly make them soft and mushy.
This can affect how they look and taste.

pg080_n0026_easy_read: The steam from the boiling water cooks the food.

pg082_n0019_easy_read: Roasting is a way of cooking food in an oven or over an open fire.

pg083_n0004_easy_read: Food for roasting is usually placed in the oven uncovered.

pg083_n0009_easy_read: The cook should follow these rules when roasting food:
pg083_n0013_easy_read: Pre-heat the oven and other heat sources to the right temperature before you put in the food.
pg083_n0014_easy_read: Pre-heating helps the food cook evenly. It also helps the food get the right texture and colour.
pg083_n0017_easy_read: Leave the roasted food for a few minutes after you take it out of the oven.
pg083_n0018_easy_read: This time lets the juices spread through the food again. This makes the dish more tasty and tender.
pg083_n0024_easy_read: Roasting brings out the natural flavours of the ingredients. This makes the food more tasty.
pg083_n0027_easy_read: Roasting gives vegetables such as potatoes a crispy and golden outside.
pg083_n0030_easy_read: Roasting needs little or no added fat or oil.
pg083_n0031_easy_read: The high heat in the oven lets the food cook in its own juices. This means you need less added fat and the dish stays moist and tasty.
pg083_n0034_easy_read: Oven roasting is a fairly simple way to cook food.
pg083_n0035_easy_read: After you season the food and put it in the oven, it needs very little attention. This lets you prepare other parts of the meal or do other tasks.
pg083_n0038_easy_read:

- meat
- poultry
- fruit
- nuts
pg083_n0039_easy_read: This means you can make many different dishes with the same cooking method.
pg083_n0042_easy_read: Roasting is healthier than frying or sautéing in oil.
pg083_n0043_easy_read: Roasting keeps the nutrients in the ingredients. It also uses very little added fat, so it is a good choice for people who want to reduce calorie intake.
pg083_n0046_easy_read: Roasting lets you make one-pan meals by putting different ingredients together in a roasting pan.
pg083_n0047_easy_read: This makes cooking simpler, cuts down the number of dishes to wash, and lets the flavours mix together.
pg083_n0050_easy_read: Roasting pans and baking trays are often easy to clean, especially if you line them with parchment paper or foil.
pg083_n0051_easy_read: This reduces the cleaning you need to do after cooking.

Roasting can cook a large amount of food at 1 time.

pg084_n0008_easy_read:
Roasted dishes with vegetables look attractive and appetising.
This makes them good for guests and special occasions.
pg084_n0014_easy_read:
Roasting takes more cooking time.
Roasting is usually slower than other cooking methods, such as frying or grilling.
pg084_n0015_easy_read:
The roasting time can be longer.
This depends on the size and type of food and on the result you want.
pg084_n0018_easy_read:
It can be hard to cook food evenly when roasting.

pg084_n0019_easy_read: You can solve this problem by using a roasting rack or by turning the food during cooking.

- the food's sugar content

pg124_n0024_easy_read: People make stock from bones, meat, fish, or vegetables, with aromatic ingredients in water.
pg124_n0025_easy_read: Some vegetables are not good for making stock.
pg124_n0026_easy_read:
These vegetables are:
- potatoes
- green leafy vegetables
pg124_n0027_easy_read: Potatoes make the stock taste sour. Green leafy vegetables make the stock taste bitter.
pg124_n0028_easy_read: People make stock by using the simmering method.
pg124_n0029_easy_read: In this method, food cooks gently and slowly.
pg124_n0030_easy_read: The slow simmering process takes flavours, nutrients, and gelatin from the ingredients. This makes a rich and savoury liquid.
pg124_n0031_easy_read: The nutritional value of stock depends on the ingredients used.
pg124_n0032_easy_read: Remember these points when preparing stock for soups:
pg124_n0035_easy_read: (a) Use clean and fresh ingredients to make stock.
pg124_n0037_easy_read: (b) Cut fish or meat into small pieces. This helps the flavour come out.
pg124_n0039_easy_read: (c) Cover the ingredients with cold water. Then cook them using the simmering method.
pg124_n0041_easy_read: (d) To make the flavour stronger, remove the lid and let the water evaporate.
pg124_n0043_easy_read: (e) Skim the stock to remove extra fat.
pg124_n0045_easy_read: (f) Strain the stock when it is ready. Cool it quickly. Store it in a cool place.
pg124_n0048_easy_read: You can keep the stock in a refrigerator for up to 3 days.
pg124_n0050_easy_read: (h) Do not warm the stock more than 1 time. This can create the right conditions for bacteria to grow.
pg124_n0052_easy_read: (i) Cook meat stock for longer than vegetable stock. This helps to get the most flavour, nutrients, and gelatin from the meat and bones.
pg125_n0005_easy_read: Soup is a tasty and nourishing liquid. People serve it at the start of a meal.
pg125_n0006_easy_read:
Soup is made from stock from:
- vegetables
- meat
- fish
- grains
- pulses
pg125_n0007_easy_read: Soup is an important starter in a meal.
pg125_n0008_easy_read: Soup helps the body make digestive juices.
pg125_n0009_easy_read: Most soups warm the body, especially in the cold season.
pg125_n0013_easy_read: Simmering is a way of cooking food gently and slowly in liquid, at a temperature just below boiling point.
pg125_n0014_easy_read: When you simmer food, keep the liquid at a temperature where small bubbles sometimes rise to the surface and break gently.
pg125_n0015_easy_read: The exact temperature for simmering is about 180°F to 200°F (82°C to 93°C).
pg125_n0016_easy_read:
Simmering is a common way of cooking many dishes, including:
- soups
- stews
- sauces
- some braised dishes
pg125_n0017_easy_read: It cooks food gently and evenly. It helps the flavours mix together and keeps the texture of the ingredients.
pg125_n0018_easy_read: When you cook by simmering, remember these points:
pg125_n0022_easy_read: Cover the pot with a lid. This keeps in moisture and heat. It helps the food cook evenly and stops too much liquid from evaporating.
pg125_n0025_easy_read: Do not open the pot unless you are sure the simmering is ready.
pg125_n0028_easy_read: Keep the temperature just below boiling.
pg125_n0029_easy_read: If the food is about to boil, add extra broth or cooking liquid to cool it.
pg125_n0032_easy_read: Use a pot that is big enough to hold all the ingredients comfortably, without overcrowding them.
pg125_n0033_easy_read: This lets the liquid move around the ingredients and helps them cook evenly.
pg125_n0036_easy_read: Stir the food from time to time while it simmers. This helps stop it from sticking or burning, especially in dishes with thick sauces or starchy ingredients.
pg125_n0039_easy_read: Simmering is a slow way of cooking, so be patient and let the ingredients cook fully.
pg125_n0040_easy_read: The cooking time will change depending on the dish and the ingredients used.
pg125_n0043_easy_read: The liquid used for simmering, such as stock, broth or sauce, is important because it adds flavour to the food.
pg125_n0044_easy_read: Season the liquid with flavourings such as herbs and spices. This improves the taste and smell of the dish.
pg125_n0047_easy_read: When simmering is finished, leave the dish for a few minutes before serving.
pg125_n0048_easy_read: This helps the flavours develop more and makes sure the food is at a good temperature for serving.
pg126_n0007_easy_read: Flavour infusion: Simmering helps the flavours of the ingredients mix together. This makes the dish taste balanced and good.
pg126_n0010_easy_read: Tenderizing: Simmering helps soften tough meat and fibrous vegetables. It breaks down the tough parts, so the food is more tender and easier to chew.
pg126_n0013_easy_read: Reduction: Simmering reduces the liquid in a dish. This makes the flavours stronger and the sauce or broth thicker.
pg126_n0016_easy_read: Even cooking: The gentle and steady heat of simmering cooks the food evenly. It helps stop the food becoming overcooked or burnt.
pg126_n0020_easy_read: Simmering is a common and useful way to cook many dishes. But it also has some disadvantages:
pg126_n0024_easy_read: Time-consuming: Simmering is a slow way of cooking. Some dishes need a long time to cook fully.
pg126_n0027_easy_read: Potential of overcooking: If you do not watch the food closely, some ingredients can overcook during simmering.
pg126_n0028_easy_read: Overcooked vegetables may lose their texture and become soft and mushy. Meat may become dry and tough.
pg126_n0031_easy_read: Evaporation of liquid: During simmering, some of the liquid in the dish can evaporate.
pg126_n0032_easy_read: This can make the flavours stronger. But it can also reduce the amount of sauce or broth, which may not be wanted in some recipes.
pg126_n0035_easy_read: Unsuitable for certain ingredients: Simmering may not suit some delicate vegetables. They can overcook and lose their bright colour, crispness, and nutritional value.
pg126_n0036_easy_read: It may change the texture and flavour.
pg126_n0039_easy_read: Slow flavour infusion: Simmering helps flavours mix together, but it may be slower than other cooking methods such as boiling or steaming.
pg126_n0040_easy_read: So, some herbs and spices may not release their flavours as quickly as wanted.

Soups can be put into 4 main groups:
- thin soups
- thick soups
- cold soups
- international soups
pg127_n0028_easy_read: People make thin soups without a thickening agent.
pg127_n0029_easy_read:
People may serve thin soups plain. They may also add solid ingredients, such as:
- vegetables
- fish
- pasta
- meat
pg127_n0030_easy_read: Thin soups can be strained or unstrained.
pg127_n0031_easy_read:
Thin soups include:
- clear soup
- broth
- consommé
pg127_n0033_easy_read: Clear soup: This soup is clear and flavoured.
pg127_n0034_easy_read:
People can make it from:
- poultry
- beef
- vegetables
pg127_n0035_easy_read: It has no solid ingredients because people strain it after making it.
pg127_n0036_easy_read: The soup is thin like a liquid.
pg127_n0037_easy_read: This soup is easy to prepare.
pg128_n0003_easy_read: Broth: This soup is like clear soup, but it is not strained.
pg128_n0004_easy_read:
Broth also has solid ingredients, such as:
- small pieces of vegetables
- fish
- meat
- rice
- pasta
- oats
pg128_n0005_easy_read: The way to make broth is similar to the way to make clear soup.
pg128_n0006_easy_read:
Examples of broth soups are:
- beef broth
- vegetable broth
- fish broth
pg128_n0011_easy_read: Consommé: This is a light, clear soup. It is made with concentrated beef or chicken stock and served hot.
pg128_n0012_easy_read: Egg white is added to the soup before serving.
pg128_n0019_easy_read:
Thick soups are made thick by using:
- flour
- cornstarch
- cream
- vegetables
- gelatines
- other ingredients
pg128_n0020_easy_read: Thick soups are opaque, unlike thin soups.
pg128_n0021_easy_read: Thick soups can have different textures and flavours. This depends on the thickening ingredients used.
pg128_n0022_easy_read:
Thick soups are grouped into these types:
- puree soup
- cream soup
- chowders
- bisque
- velouté
pg129_n0004_easy_read: Puree soups: People make these soups by simmering fresh or dried starchy vegetables in stock or water.
pg129_n0005_easy_read: After that, people blend or crush the vegetables to make a thick soup called puree soup.
pg129_n0006_easy_read: For pureed soup, people cook the ingredients until they are soft. Then they blend them until smooth. This makes the soup thick and there are no visible pieces of food.
pg129_n0007_easy_read:
People can make puree soup from:
- rice
- dried legumes, such as peas
- fresh starchy vegetables, such as potatoes
pg129_n0008_easy_read:
Some common ingredients for puree soups are:
- tomatoes
- carrots
- potatoes
- peas
- cauliflower
pg129_n0009_easy_read:
People can also use fruit in sweet puree soups, for example:
- apples
- pears
- pumpkins
pg129_n0014_easy_read: Cream soups: Cream soups are soups with a rich, creamy texture.
pg129_n0015_easy_read:
People make these soups by adding dairy products to the soup, such as:
- cream
- milk
- butter
pg129_n0016_easy_read: These soups are smooth and soft.
pg129_n0017_easy_read:
People can make cream soups with different ingredients, including:
- vegetables
- cream
- seafood
- poultry
- meat
pg129_n0018_easy_read:
People season cream soups with:
- herbs
- spices
- other flavourings
This improves the taste.
pg129_n0019_easy_read:
Examples of cream soup are:
- tomato soup
- mushroom soup
- chicken soup
pg129_n0020_easy_read: Figure 5.20 shows cream of mushroom soup.
pg130_n0003_easy_read:
Chowders:
Chowders are thick soups with large pieces of food.
They usually have fish, seafood, poultry, or vegetables in a creamy base.
pg130_n0004_easy_read:
Chowders usually have herbs and spices for flavour.
Sometimes they also have bacon or salt pork.
pg130_n0006_easy_read: Examples of chowders are seafood chowder soup and maize chowder soup.
pg130_n0007_easy_read:
Figure 5.21 shows maize chowder soup.
Maize chowder soup is also called corn chowder.
pg130_n0011_easy_read:
Bisque:
Bisque is a soup made from shellfish.
It has different ingredients added for flavour.
pg130_n0012_easy_read:
Traditionally, bisque is made with:
- lobster
- crab
- shrimp
- crawfish
There are also versions with:
- vegetables
- mushrooms
- other seafood
pg130_n0013_easy_read: Bisque soup is tasty, but it is expensive.
pg130_n0014_easy_read: The soup may have small cubes of the seafood used on top.
pg130_n0015_easy_read: It is made thick with cooked rice and finished with cream.
pg130_n0016_easy_read: Examples of bisque soups are lobster bisque and prawn bisque.
pg131_n0004_easy_read: Velouté: A velouté is a thick soup.
pg131_n0005_easy_read:
A velouté is made from:
- meat
- poultry
- fish
- vegetables
pg131_n0006_easy_read: The stock used gives the soup its flavour.
pg131_n0007_easy_read:
The soup is made thick with a blond.
A blond is made by cooking equal amounts of wheat flour and butter over medium heat until it is light brown.
pg131_n0008_easy_read: Egg yolks and cream are added to this soup just before serving.
pg131_n0009_easy_read:
Velouté is very versatile.
It is used as a base for many dishes, as a sauce and as a soup.
pg131_n0010_easy_read:
The name of the soup depends on the stock used.
For example, chicken velouté soup is made with chicken.
pg131_n0014_easy_read:
Cold soups, also called chilled soups, are refreshing and tasty.
People often have them in hot weather.
pg131_n0015_easy_read: Cold soups are a special category because they are served chilled.
pg131_n0016_easy_read:
Hot soups become cold soups after they are chilled.
Small changes are made to their consistency and flavour.
pg131_n0017_easy_read: Cold soups can be thickened with starches.
pg131_n0018_easy_read: Cold soups are more popular in warm weather.
pg131_n0019_easy_read:
Traditional hot soups are served warm.
Cold soups are meant to be eaten cold or at room temperature.
pg131_n0023_easy_read: International soups, also called national soups, include many flavourful and unique soups from different countries and cultures around the world.
pg131_n0024_easy_read: International soups represent the region they come from.
pg131_n0025_easy_read:
Each soup reflects:
- the cooking traditions
- the regional ingredients
- the local preferences
of its country of origin.
pg131_n0026_easy_read: International soups strongly reflect a particular culture and history.
pg131_n0027_easy_read: People value international soups as a symbol of national identity.
pg131_n0028_easy_read:
Examples are:
- scotch broth from Scotland
- green turtle soup from England
- French onion soup from France

pg132_n0016_easy_read: A good soup should have these qualities:
pg132_n0020_easy_read:
The soup should have a rich flavour, depending on the ingredients used.
Use enough seasoning to bring out the flavour.
pg132_n0023_easy_read: The soup should not be greasy.

pg132_n0027_easy_read: A good soup should be balanced and nourishing.

pg132_n0031_easy_read: A good soup should look appealing.

pg132_n0035_easy_read: A soup may be thick and have the right consistency, depending on its type and on the ingredients and preparation.
pg132_n0036_easy_read: The soup should not have lumps.
pg132_n0039_easy_read: The ingredients should be finely chopped and easy to fit onto a spoon.
pg132_n0042_easy_read:
The ingredients should be well balanced.
Each ingredient should add to the whole dish and should not overpower the others.
pg132_n0044_easy_read: Note: Do not overcook the soup. This helps the soup keep its flavour.
pg132_n0045_easy_read: If you use stock to make the soup, the stock should be fresh and well flavoured.
pg132_n0046_easy_read:
You can serve soup with foods such as:

pg134_n0010_easy_read: Pulses, nuts and oil seeds are foods. They contain nutrients such as protein, fat, minerals and vitamins. Our bodies need these nutrients.
pg134_n0011_easy_read: Pulses and nuts also contain dietary fibre. Dietary fibre is good for the body.
pg134_n0012_easy_read: People use pulses, nuts and oil seeds to make different dishes with different cooking methods.
pg134_n0013_easy_read: Pulses, nuts and oil seeds come in different shapes, sizes and colours.
pg134_n0014_easy_read:
In this chapter, you will learn about:
- pulses, nuts and oil seeds
- the nutritive value of pulses and nuts
- their uses
- methods of cooking them
pg134_n0015_easy_read: The skills you develop will help you use pulses, nuts and oil seeds to make different dishes. This can improve health and help you earn income.
pg134_n0018_easy_read: Different ways to use pulses, nuts and oil seeds
pg134_n0022_easy_read: Pulses are dry seeds that people can eat.
pg134_n0024_easy_read:
People value pulses because they:
- are nutritious
- are affordable
- are easy to find
pg134_n0025_easy_read:
Pulses:
- are low in fat
- are high in protein
- are rich in dietary fibre
Pulses are a very good source of plant-based protein and other important nutrients.
pg134_n0026_easy_read:
Commonly used pulses are:
- beans
- cowpeas
- soya beans
- chickpeas
- green grams
- lima beans
- lentils
- Bambara nuts
- pigeon peas
pg134_n0027_easy_read: Pulses have an outer protective layer. This layer is called the seed coat or skin.
pg134_n0028_easy_read: Over time, the seed coat of pulses can become harder and less permeable. This happens especially during storage, when temperature and humidity change. Then the pulses become difficult to cook.
pg134_n0029_easy_read: Figure 6.1 shows different types of pulses.
pg136_n0005_easy_read:
Pulses contain important nutrients, such as:
- proteins of low biological value
- B-vitamins, except riboflavin
- minerals such as iron, potassium and magnesium
pg136_n0006_easy_read: Pulses contain carbohydrates, but only small amounts.
pg136_n0007_easy_read: Pulses are also low in fat. Soya beans are different. Soya beans are a very good source of fat.
pg136_n0008_easy_read: Pulses are also high in dietary fibre.
pg136_n0012_easy_read:
People use pulses to make:
- gravies
- stews
- soups
- bites
pg136_n0013_easy_read:
People can also use pulses to make:
- salads
- desserts
pg136_n0014_easy_read: People can grind pulses into a fine powder. They use this powder to thicken food and add extra protein to the meal.
pg136_n0015_easy_read: In vegetarian meals, cooked pulses are the main source of protein.
pg136_n0016_easy_read:
People can also serve pulses with other starchy foods, such as:
- ugali
- rice
- pasta
pg136_n0021_easy_read: Nuts are very nutritious and healthy foods. They provide many essential nutrients and health benefits.
pg136_n0022_easy_read:
Nuts are good sources of:
- proteins
- minerals
- vitamins
pg136_n0023_easy_read: Nuts also contain a lot of fat. This fat may help brain health and brain function.
pg136_n0024_easy_read:
There are different kinds of nuts, such as:
- cashew nuts
- groundnuts
- walnuts
- Oysternut
- Brazil nuts
- almonds
pg136_n0026_easy_read: Oil seeds contain a lot of oil.
pg136_n0027_easy_read: Oil seeds are also called oil-rich seeds.
pg136_n0028_easy_read: People extract oil from oil seeds. They use this oil for different purposes, mainly as edible oil for cooking.
pg136_n0029_easy_read: In contrast, people can grind whole oil seeds into flour or fine powder and use them in cooking.
pg136_n0030_easy_read:
Examples of oil seeds are:
- sunflower
- sesame (or simsim)
- pumpkin seeds
- cotton seeds

Nuts also contain many vitamins and minerals:
- folate

- vitamin E
- vitamin B6
- magnesium
- zinc
- iron

pg138_n0026_easy_read: Some nuts contain phosphorus and potassium.
pg138_n0027_easy_read:
Walnuts contain a lot of unsaturated fats, such as omega-3 fatty acids.
These fats help brain and heart health.

pg138_n0030_easy_read: Oil seeds do not contain much carbohydrate, but they contain a lot of B-vitamins.

Oil seeds add important nutrients to the diet.

pg138_n0037_easy_read: Nuts can be used in baking foods such as biscuits and cakes.

pg139_n0006_easy_read:
You can use several methods to cook pulses.
The method depends on the type of pulse and the result you want.
pg139_n0007_easy_read:
You can cook pulses by:
- boiling
- stewing
- pressure cooking
pg139_n0008_easy_read:
Nuts are tasty and healthy ingredients.

So, you can cook nuts in different ways, such as:
- frying
- roasting

pg139_n0011_easy_read:
Pressure cooking method:
This is a moist heat method.
It uses a pressure cooker to cook food with high-pressure steam.
pg139_n0012_easy_read:
Put the food and a suitable amount of water into the pressure cooker.
The amount of water depends on the type of food.
Then close the cooker with its special tight-fitting lid.
pg139_n0013_easy_read: When the water boils, it makes steam.
pg139_n0014_easy_read: This process increases the pressure inside the cooker.
pg139_n0015_easy_read: The higher temperature and pressure cook the food very quickly.
pg139_n0016_easy_read: During cooking, the cooker can control and keep the pressure needed to cook the food.
pg139_n0017_easy_read:
After cooking, leave the pressure cooker for a few minutes.
This lowers the steam pressure.
Then you can open the cooker safely.
pg139_n0018_easy_read:
Pulses that are suitable for this method include:
- dried beans
- chickpeas
- lentils
pg139_n0033_easy_read: Each part of the pressure cooker works as follows:
pg139_n0035_easy_read:
Pressure regulator:
This keeps the pressure needed to cook food.
pg139_n0037_easy_read:
Vent pipe:
This lets extra steam escape.
This keeps the right pressure inside.
pg139_n0039_easy_read:
Air vent or cover lock:
This releases air from the pressure cooker automatically.
pg140_n0003_easy_read: Sealing ring: It is a round piece of rubber around the inside part of the cover.
pg140_n0004_easy_read: The sealing ring makes a seal between the cover and the body of the cooker during cooking.
pg140_n0006_easy_read: Overpressure regulator: This lets extra pressure out of the cooker.
pg140_n0008_easy_read: Cover handle: You use this to remove the lid from the cooker or to open the cooker.
pg140_n0010_easy_read: Body handle: This handle is attached to the body of the cooker. It fits under the cover handle.
pg140_n0012_easy_read: Cover or lid: This locks onto the body of the cooker.
pg140_n0013_easy_read: The cover or lid has a sealing ring so it closes properly.
pg140_n0019_easy_read: Use enough water so that enough steam builds up inside the cooker.
pg140_n0022_easy_read: Put no more than 2/3 of the solid food capacity and no more than 1/2 of the liquid capacity in the cooker.
pg140_n0023_easy_read: If you put in more than these amounts, the control valve will fail.
pg140_n0026_easy_read: Make sure the lid is locked correctly before you start cooking.
pg140_n0029_easy_read: Put the pressure gauge in place. Then let the pressure build up to the level you want.
pg140_n0030_easy_read: A steady hissing sound means that pressure has built up.
pg140_n0033_easy_read: Lower the heat to keep the right pressure. Cook for the correct time.
pg140_n0034_easy_read: Start timing when the cooker reaches the right pressure.
pg140_n0037_easy_read: When the cooking time is finished, turn off the heat. Let the pressure go down by leaving the cooker at room temperature or by pouring a gentle stream of cold water over it.
pg140_n0038_easy_read: Do not try to open the lid or remove the pressure gauge before the pressure returns to normal.
pg140_n0045_easy_read: It uses fuel in a cost-effective way. It also needs less time and energy to cook food. This lowers energy use and cooking costs.
pg140_n0048_easy_read: It is good for pulses with hard coats because pressure cooking makes them tender easily.
pg141_n0005_easy_read:
Pressure cooking means you do not need to watch the food all the time or stir it often.
You can set it up and leave it until the food is cooked.
pg141_n0008_easy_read:
You can use a pressure cooker for many dishes, including:
- beans
- cowpeas
- pigeon peas
pg141_n0011_easy_read:
A pressure cooker cooks food in less time and uses very little liquid.
This helps the food keep more nutrients, such as vitamins and minerals.
Longer cooking methods may cause nutrient loss.
pg141_n0014_easy_read:
A pressure cooker uses less energy and keeps more water.
Because of this, it has less impact on the environment overall.
pg141_n0020_easy_read: High-quality pressure cookers can cost more than traditional cooking pots.

Modern pressure cookers have built-in safety features.

pg154_n0009_easy_read: Proper nutrition helps the body stay active and work well.
pg154_n0010_easy_read: Proper nutrition comes from eating a balanced meal. A balanced meal is needed for life.
pg154_n0011_easy_read: A person with proper nutrition can take part in different economic activities and improve his or her standard of living.
pg154_n0012_easy_read:
In this chapter, you will learn:
- what proper nutrition means
- why proper nutrition is important for health
- how diet, health and physical activities are linked
pg154_n0013_easy_read: You will also learn about different eating disorders.
pg154_n0014_easy_read: The skills you develop will help you make informed food choices. They will also help you prevent Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and eating disorders. You will also be able to educate the wider community.
pg154_n0021_easy_read: Proper nutrition means eating a balanced meal and doing regular physical activities, such as running and walking.
pg154_n0022_easy_read: Good health depends on proper nutrition.
pg154_n0023_easy_read: Proper nutrition is essential for keeping good health and well-being throughout life.
pg154_n0024_easy_read: Making informed food choices and healthy eating habits are important steps. They help improve overall health and prevent nutrition-related health disorders.
pg154_n0026_easy_read: Proper nutrition is also important for a healthy lifestyle.
pg154_n0027_easy_read: A healthy lifestyle means a person's way of living. It includes behaviours and choices that lower the risk of illness or early death.
pg154_n0028_easy_read: A healthy lifestyle includes these aspects:
pg154_n0032_easy_read: Moderate use of sweetened foods and drinks: These foods contain large
pg155_n0005_easy_read:
Sweet foods and drinks can cause health problems, such as:
- overweight
- obesity
- heart attack
- stroke
- kidney stones
- some types of cancer
pg155_n0006_easy_read: It is best to use sweetened foods and drinks in moderate amounts.
pg155_n0010_easy_read:
Use junk food as little as possible.
These foods are high in fat, sugar and salt.
They are low in protein, vitamins and minerals.
pg155_n0011_easy_read:
Examples of junk food include:
- carbonated drinks
- gum
- fried fast foods
pg155_n0014_easy_read:
Do not use tobacco and alcohol.
Tobacco products that people smoke, chew or sniff are harmful to health.
They increase the risk of non-communicable diseases.
pg155_n0017_easy_read:
Achieve and maintain a healthy body weight.
A healthy body weight helps a person feel fit and energetic.
pg155_n0018_easy_read: A healthy body weight also reduces the risk of non-communicable diseases.
pg155_n0021_easy_read:
Maintain personal and food hygiene and safety.
It is important to keep good personal and food hygiene and safety when preparing food.
This helps prevent illness.
pg155_n0025_easy_read: Proper nutrition has several benefits for our bodies:
pg155_n0027_easy_read:
Strengthening the body’s immune system:
Proper nutrition builds the body’s immunity.
pg155_n0028_easy_read: A body with strong immunity does not get diseases easily.
pg155_n0029_easy_read: Strong immunity helps a person take part actively in different productive activities.
pg155_n0031_easy_read:
Maintain the right energy level in the body.
The body needs energy for different activities.
pg155_n0033_easy_read: Eating a balanced meal helps the body get the energy it needs for different functions.
pg155_n0035_easy_read:
Improves physical and mental health:
Proper nutrition makes the body active and strong.
pg155_n0036_easy_read:
Eating meals with enough nutrients helps a person have a healthy mind.
This improves thinking and reasoning.
pg155_n0038_easy_read:
Helps a person live longer:
Eating meals rich in nutrients increases lifespan.
pg155_n0039_easy_read: Healthy eating makes the body strong and helps prevent some diseases.
pg155_n0040_easy_read: It is better to follow good eating habits to stay healthier.
pg155_n0042_easy_read:
Helps maintain a healthy body weight:
Proper nutrition helps a person achieve the required body weight.
pg155_n0043_easy_read: A person can achieve the required body weight through enough nutrient intake and regular physical activity.
pg156_n0003_easy_read:
Improves growth and development:
Good nutrition is very important during growth and development, especially in childhood and adolescence.
pg156_n0004_easy_read: Essential nutrients help the body grow properly.
pg156_n0005_easy_read: Not getting enough food and nutrients during childhood can lead to stunted growth.
pg156_n0007_easy_read:
Improves bone health:
A healthy meal with a lot of calcium and vitamin D is very important for good bone health. It can also help prevent conditions such as osteomalacia. Osteomalacia means the bones become soft and weak because the body does not get enough vitamin D, calcium or phosphorus.
pg156_n0008_easy_read:
Getting enough of these nutrients, and other nutrients that support bones, is essential for strong and healthy bones throughout life:
- vitamin K
- magnesium
- protein
pg156_n0012_easy_read: A diet is the food that a person usually eats.
pg156_n0013_easy_read: People sometimes change their diet to control how much of certain foods they eat. They do this to prevent, treat or manage some health conditions.
pg156_n0014_easy_read: This type of diet is called a special diet.
pg156_n0015_easy_read:
Examples of special diets are:
- low-fat diets
- low-carbohydrate diets
- low-salt diets
- low-sugar diets
pg156_n0017_easy_read: Diet, physical activity and health are closely linked.
pg156_n0018_easy_read: When diet, physical activity and health are balanced, they have a positive effect on a person's overall well-being.
pg156_n0019_easy_read: Physical activity is any body movement made by skeletal muscles. This movement uses energy.
pg156_n0020_easy_read: Doing regular physical activity lowers the risk of becoming overweight or obese. Being overweight or obese can increase the risk of non-communicable diseases, also called chronic diseases, such as coronary heart disease, type 2 diabetes and some cancers.
pg156_n0021_easy_read:
Examples of physical activities are:
- walking
- running
- dancing
- swimming
- gardening
pg156_n0023_easy_read: The following points show the relationship between diet, physical activity and health:
pg156_n0027_easy_read: A balanced meal and regular physical activity are very important for a healthy body weight.
pg156_n0028_easy_read: A nutrient-rich meal and regular physical activity can prevent too much weight gain. This helps a person keep an ideal body weight.
pg156_n0031_easy_read: A balanced meal and physical activity help heart health.
pg156_n0032_easy_read:
Low-fat and low-sodium meals, and regular physical activity, can:
- lower blood pressure
- reduce cholesterol
- lower the risk of heart disease
pg156_n0035_easy_read: Proper nutrition, especially enough calcium and vitamin D, is essential for good teeth and bone health.
pg156_n0036_easy_read: When proper nutrition is combined with physical activities, it also supports bone strength and overall well-being.
pg157_n0006_easy_read:
A balanced meal with different vitamins and minerals supports the immune system.
This helps the body resist infections and illnesses better.
pg157_n0007_easy_read: Regular physical activity is also linked to a stronger immune system.
pg157_n0011_easy_read: A balanced meal and physical activity have a big effect on mental health.
pg157_n0012_easy_read:
Foods rich in nutrients and regular physical activity can:
- lower the risk of depression
- lower the risk of anxiety
- improve mood
- boost thinking skills
pg157_n0016_easy_read: Good nutrition and regular physical activity can prevent or manage non-communicable diseases, such as type 2 diabetes and some cancers.
pg157_n0017_easy_read: A healthy lifestyle lowers the risk of developing these conditions.
pg157_n0021_easy_read: A balanced meal and regular physical activity improve sleep.
pg157_n0022_easy_read:
A balanced meal and regular physical activity help people sleep better.
This supports overall physical health.
pg157_n0026_easy_read:
A healthy lifestyle with balanced meals and physical activity is linked to a longer life.
It also lowers the risk of early death.

An eating disorder is a serious health condition.
It happens when a person avoids food or eats too much food.
pg159_n0006_easy_read: An eating disorder affects a person’s weight and body shape.
pg159_n0007_easy_read:
This can lead to unhealthy eating habits.
These habits can seriously harm physical health and the way the body works.
pg159_n0008_easy_read: Eating disorders are more common in teenage girls and young women than in boys and men.
pg159_n0009_easy_read:
If eating disorders are not managed well, they can cause long-term problems.
In some cases, they can lead to death.
pg159_n0010_easy_read:
The most common eating disorders are:
- anorexia nervosa
- bulimia nervosa
- binge-eating
- pica
pg159_n0014_easy_read: Eating disorders can affect people of all ages, backgrounds and genders.
pg159_n0015_easy_read:
However, eating disorders often start during adolescence.
They can also start during childhood or later in life.
pg159_n0016_easy_read:
Some factors can lead to eating disorders.
These are:
pg159_n0021_easy_read:
Genetics and family history:
Eating disorders are more likely in people whose parents or siblings have an eating disorder.
pg159_n0025_easy_read:
Gender:
Eating disorders are more common in females than in males because females are more aware of their body image.
pg159_n0026_easy_read: However, eating disorders can affect people of any gender.
pg159_n0030_easy_read:
Age:
Eating disorders often start during adolescence and early adulthood.
pg159_n0031_easy_read:
Pressure to match society’s beauty standards can increase the risk.
Changes in body image during these stages of development can also increase the risk.
pg159_n0035_easy_read:
Body image dissatisfaction:
Having a poor body image or feeling unhappy with your appearance can be a major risk factor for developing an eating disorder.
pg159_n0039_easy_read:
Other mental health issues:
Stress, anxiety, depression and other mental health issues can increase the chance of an eating disorder.
pg159_n0043_easy_read:
A history of weight bullying:
People who have been bullied about their weight are more likely to develop eating disorders.
pg159_n0044_easy_read:
This includes people who have been made to feel ashamed of their weight by:
- peers
- healthcare professionals
- coaches
- family members
pg159_n0048_easy_read:
Social media pressure:
Seeing unrealistic body images and unhealthy messages about dieting and appearance on social media can affect body image and increase the risk of eating disorders.
pg160_n0003_easy_read: (viii) Occupations: Some jobs can increase the risk of eating disorders because a certain body image is seen as ideal.
pg160_n0004_easy_read:
Some jobs that may increase the risk of eating disorders are:
- athletics
- fashion modelling
- acting
- dancing
- performing arts
pg160_n0006_easy_read: Note: Having 1 or more of these factors does not always mean a person will develop an eating disorder. But these factors may increase the risk.
pg160_n0010_easy_read: People with eating disorders often show a range of physical, emotional and behavioural signs.
pg160_n0011_easy_read: It is important to remember that each person with an eating disorder is different.
pg160_n0013_easy_read: These are some common characteristics seen in people with eating disorders:
pg160_n0015_easy_read: Distorted body image: Some people with eating disorders have a distorted view of their body size and shape.
pg160_n0016_easy_read: For example, they may think they are overweight even when they are very underweight.
pg160_n0018_easy_read: Restrictive eating patterns: In a condition like anorexia nervosa, people greatly limit how much food they eat. This can lead to major weight loss and malnutrition.
pg160_n0019_easy_read: They may avoid certain food groups or greatly limit their total calorie intake.
pg160_n0021_easy_read:
Changes in eating habits: There may be a clear change in eating habits, such as:
- eating alone
- avoiding eating in public with other people
- making excuses to avoid eating
pg160_n0022_easy_read: People with binge eating disorder eat excessively.
pg160_n0024_easy_read: Social withdrawal: People with eating disorders may stop taking part in social activities and may isolate themselves from friends and family.
pg160_n0026_easy_read:
Emotional and behavioural changes: Common emotional signs are:
- mood swings
- anxiety
- depression
- feelings of guilt
- feelings of shame
pg160_n0028_easy_read:
Development of physical signs: Physical signs of eating disorders can include:
- rapid weight loss
- dizziness
- weakness
- hair loss
- dry skin
- changes in menstrual patterns (amenorrhea) among women
pg160_n0030_easy_read: Excessive exercise: Some people may exercise too much as a way to control their weight and shape.
pg161_n0005_easy_read:
Eating disorders are a group of related conditions.
They involve extreme problems with food and weight.
Each disorder has its own symptoms and its own criteria for diagnosis.
pg161_n0006_easy_read:
Common eating disorders include:
- anorexia nervosa
- bulimia nervosa
- binge eating
- pica
pg161_n0010_easy_read:
Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder.
A person with anorexia nervosa has:
- a very low body weight
- a strong fear of gaining weight
- a false view of their own weight
pg161_n0011_easy_read:
Anorexia nervosa involves limiting foods that give energy.
This can lead to a body weight that is much too low for the person's age, sex and height.
pg161_n0012_easy_read: This restriction often happens because the person has a strong fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even when their body weight is already low.
pg161_n0013_easy_read: Anorexia nervosa is probably a well-known eating disorder.
pg161_n0014_easy_read:
Anorexia nervosa usually starts during adolescence or young adulthood.
It affects more women than men.
pg161_n0015_easy_read: People with anorexia nervosa usually think they are overweight, even when they are dangerously underweight.
pg161_n0016_easy_read:
People with anorexia nervosa often:
- check their body weight all the time
- avoid certain foods
- greatly limit the calories they eat
pg161_n0020_easy_read:
Bulimia nervosa is an eating disorder.
It means eating a large amount of food in a short time.
pg161_n0021_easy_read:
After this, the person tries to stop weight gain.
They may:
- make themselves vomit
- use diet pills or other medicines
- fast
- do too much exercise
pg161_n0022_easy_read:
If bulimia nervosa is not treated, it can lead to a lack of nutrients.
It can also cause complications that may be fatal.
pg161_n0023_easy_read:
People with bulimia nervosa are usually ashamed of their behaviour.
They often hide this condition from other people.
pg161_n0027_easy_read:
Binge eating is an eating disorder.
It means eating large amounts of food in a short time, like bulimia nervosa.
pg161_n0028_easy_read: However, people with this condition do not make themselves vomit, do excessive exercise, or do other behaviours like this.
pg161_n0029_easy_read: People with this condition feel that they do not have control over their eating.
pg161_n0030_easy_read: They usually eat quickly until they feel uncomfortably full, even when they are not physically hungry.
pg161_n0031_easy_read:
These people often feel:
- guilt
- shame
- distress
pg161_n0032_easy_read:
People with BED often feel embarrassed about how much food they eat.
Because of this, they often refuse to eat in public.
pg161_n0033_easy_read: These people often eat too much food and may not choose nutritious foods.
pg161_n0034_easy_read: This may increase the risk of obesity and non-communicable diseases, such as heart disease and type 2 diabetes.
pg162_n0005_easy_read:
Pica is an eating disorder.
It means eating things that are not food and have no nutritional value, such as soil, chalk, charcoal or ice.
pg162_n0006_easy_read: Pica is most common in children and pregnant women.
pg162_n0007_easy_read:
Pica can be dangerous.
It can cause serious health problems, such as:
- poisoning
- infections
- gut injuries
- nutrient deficiency

pg162_n0021_easy_read:
To control eating disorders, people need to take action together.
These actions must deal with the physical, psychological and emotional parts of the condition.
pg162_n0022_easy_read: Eating disorders can seriously affect a person's physical and emotional well-being.
pg162_n0023_easy_read:
There is no exact way to prevent eating disorders.
But healthy eating habits can help.
pg162_n0024_easy_read: Each person's recovery from an eating disorder is different.
pg162_n0025_easy_read: So it is very important to get professional help from healthcare providers who specialise in treating eating disorders.
pg162_n0026_easy_read: Acting early on these problems can greatly improve the chances of successful recovery.
pg162_n0027_easy_read: The following are ways to control eating disorders:
pg162_n0031_easy_read:
A healthcare professional may do a full medical assessment.
This helps them:
- check the person's overall health
- find any medical problems caused by the eating disorder
- make a suitable treatment plan
pg162_n0032_easy_read:
Medical treatment may include:
- treating any nutritional conditions
- stabilising weight
- managing any physical health problems linked to the eating disorder
pg163_n0006_easy_read:
People and communities need information about:
- nutrition
- eating habits
- the importance of a balanced diet
pg163_n0007_easy_read:
Nutrition education aims to:
- promote healthy eating habits
- improve overall health
- prevent illnesses linked to diet
- encourage good food choices
pg163_n0008_easy_read: Including family members in nutrition education can improve understanding and management of eating disorders.
pg163_n0009_easy_read:
Nutritionists can provide nutrition education in:
- communities
- schools
- health facilities
pg163_n0010_easy_read: However, peer group educators can also be effective.
pg163_n0011_easy_read:
Media can be used to create awareness about nutrition, for example:
- television
- radio
- posters
- fliers
- social networks

Psychotherapy, also called talk therapy, is an important part of treatment for eating disorders.
Mental health professionals do this therapy.
pg164_n0008_easy_read:
Psychotherapy involves regular personal talks.
These talks help a person change unhealthy behaviour.
pg164_n0009_easy_read: Family-based therapy is one of the treatments often used for eating disorders.
pg164_n0010_easy_read:
These therapies can help people develop:
- healthier thoughts
- healthier feelings
- better behaviours about food, body image, and self-esteem
pg164_n0014_easy_read: Working with a nutritionist or a registered dietitian who specialises in eating disorders can help a person create a balanced and healthy meal plan.
pg164_n0015_easy_read:
Nutrition counselling helps people build a healthier relationship with food.
It also helps them eat regularly and improve their behaviour.
pg164_n0019_easy_read: Eating disorders often happen with other mental health conditions, such as depression and anxiety.
pg164_n0020_easy_read: It is important to identify and treat any existing disorders for full recovery.
pg164_n0024_easy_read: It is important to identify and reduce triggers that increase disordered eating behaviours.
pg164_n0025_easy_read:
This includes limiting exposure to:
- social media
- content that promotes unrealistic body ideas
- content that promotes unhealthy eating behaviours
